item.title: FG’s ₦50,000 NERSI Relief: Who Qualifies, How Selection Works, and How to Claim Safely
item.dc:creator: 9jaBeacon Desk
item.description: The Federal Government’s National Emergency Relief and Stabilisation Intervention (NERSI) is paying ₦50,000 to selected vulnerable households. Beneficiaries are drawn from the National Social Register and NIN records — not open applications. Verified quotes, payment path, and anti-scam steps.
item.content:encoded:
Abuja — Nigeria’s Federal Government has begun paying a ₦50,000 cash relief to selected vulnerable households under the National Emergency Relief and Stabilisation Intervention (NERSI), a presidential programme announced by the Ministry of Humanitarian Affairs and Poverty Reduction.

The scheme is designed to ease pressure from high food and essential-goods prices. Officials stress that it is not an open application portal: people are chosen from existing government databases, contacted in phases, and paid into mobile wallets after they consent.

What officials announced

Minister of Humanitarian Affairs and Poverty Reduction Dr Bernard Doro, in the ministry’s 30 October 2026 commencement statement, described NERSI as a presidential initiative for immediate relief.

“Under this intervention, eligible beneficiaries will receive ₦50,000 monthly, providing direct assistance to help meet essential needs and ease the burden of living costs.”

— Dr Bernard Doro, Minister of Humanitarian Affairs and Poverty Reduction

He linked the programme to President Bola Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda and said the ministry would deliver it “with dignity, transparency and accountability.”

Programme materials and mainstream reporting also quote the intervention’s plain rule on the money itself:

“It is a grant from the Federal Government. You do not pay it back.”

— NERSI programme guidance, as reported by Punch from the ministry’s NERSI materials

“₦50,000. The full amount goes into your wallet. Nothing is deducted.”

— Programme guidance cited by Punch (5 November 2026)

Who is selected — and who is not

According to the ministry’s NERSI eligibility notes (as reported by Punch, Tribune, Business Times and others):

  • Beneficiaries are drawn from verified national identity records (NIN / NIMC) and the National Social Register (NSR).
  • Households are screened toward poor and vulnerable groups; being on the register does not automatically guarantee payment.
  • Selection is described as based on need, covering all six geopolitical zones, without religion, ethnicity or political affiliation as the test.
  • You cannot apply through a public form, and no agent can add you to the list for a fee.

“Beneficiaries are selected from verified national identity records and the national social register, then screened to reach poor and vulnerable households.”

— NERSI eligibility text, as published via Punch Online

“You cannot apply, and no one can add you to the list.”

— Programme statement, Punch (5 November 2026)

The National Social Register is coordinated under Nigeria’s social safety-net architecture and holds records on tens of millions of people; reporting cites figures above 70 million Nigerians captured in related NSR systems. Payments are rolling out in phases — so not receiving an SMS yet does not always mean permanent exclusion from a later batch.

How payment works

  1. Selected people get an SMS from an approved payment provider asking for consent.
  2. They confirm (often via USSD or in-app prompt).
  3. Funds are credited to a mobile wallet / account linked to their identity records.

Doro said the SMS consent step is genuine when it comes from the approved providers, and that payment follows consent.

Providers repeatedly named in official and national coverage include: ALAT by Wema, MoMo Payment Service Bank, NairaGram, OPay and Moniepoint. USSD shortcodes circulating in the press include forms such as *945*23# (ALAT), *671*0# (MoMo), *726*00# (NairaGram), *955*20# (OPay) and Moniepoint variants reported as *5573*27# / *557*327#. Always confirm the exact code inside the official SMS or the provider’s own app/help channel — scammers recycle fake codes.

Security: what the government warns

“Beneficiaries are not required to apply, pay any fee or register through any agent to receive support. Never share your PIN or BVN with anyone. If you are unsure about any message, or anyone asks you for money, call the official NERSI helpline on 0700-022-2222.”

— Dr Bernard Doro, NERSI commencement statement (30 October 2026), as carried by Tribune and others

Separate fact-checks in the same news cycle have already flagged unrelated fake “₦50,000 youth grant” WhatsApp links impersonating private foundations — a reminder that viral grant messages are a favourite phishing vector whenever a real FG programme is in the headlines.

Practical checklist

  • Do not pay anyone to “put your name” on NERSI.
  • Do not share BVN, bank PIN, OTP or NIN photos with strangers or random links.
  • If selected, wait for the provider SMS, then confirm only through the channel named in that message or the provider’s official app.
  • If unsure, use the published helpline 0700-022-2222.
  • If USSD says you are not selected, that can mean “not in this phase” — not always a permanent “never.”

9jaBeacon Money Desk — synthesised from multi-outlet coverage of the Federal Ministry of Humanitarian Affairs and Poverty Reduction / NERSI materials as reported by Punch, Guardian, Tribune, Nairametrics, BBC Pidgin and Legit.ng (30 October – 6 November 2026). Cross-check live SMS text and provider apps for operational details that may change by batch.

item.title: ₦50,000 Grant Scams Are Spreading: Official NERSI Rules, Helpline, and How to Stay Safe
item.dc:creator: 9jaBeacon Desk
item.description: As FG’s NERSI ₦50,000 relief rolls out, fraudsters push fake registration links and agent fees. Official ministerial warnings, helpline 0700-022-2222, and how to spot phishing — including debunked fake youth-grant messages.
item.content:encoded:
Security desk — Every time the Federal Government announces a cash programme, a parallel market of fake forms, paid “slots,” and phishing links appears within hours. The ₦50,000 NERSI relief is no exception.

This guide sticks to verified official warnings and confirmed red flags from national media and fact-checkers in the current cycle (late October – early November 2026).

The government’s own security line

When Humanitarian Affairs Minister Dr Bernard Doro announced NERSI’s commencement on 30 October 2026, the statement did not only explain payments — it warned the public:

“Beneficiaries are not required to apply, pay any fee or register through any agent to receive support.”

— Dr Bernard Doro, Federal Ministry of Humanitarian Affairs and Poverty Reduction

“Never share your PIN or BVN with anyone. If you are unsure about any message, or anyone asks you for money, call the official NERSI helpline on 0700-022-2222.”

— Same ministerial statement, as published by Tribune Online and other national outlets

That is the core rule set. Anything that demands a fee, a “processing charge,” or remote control of your phone fails those tests.

How real NERSI contact is described

  • Selection comes from National Social Register + verified NIN records — not from a viral Google Form.
  • Contact is expected via SMS from approved payment providers (widely named: ALAT, MoMo PSB, NairaGram, OPay, Moniepoint).
  • You consent, then funds go to a wallet/account — programme text says the full ₦50,000 with no deduction.
  • Payments move in phases; delayed SMS is not automatically a scam, but a stranger’s “I can fast-track you” offer is.

“You cannot apply, and no one can add you to the list.”

— NERSI programme guidance, Punch (5 November 2026)

Scam patterns already seen this week

  1. Fake registration links — short URLs asking for NIN, BVN, OTP “to unlock ₦50,000.”
  2. Agent fees — “Pay ₦2,000 / ₦5,000 and I will put your name.” Official text says no fee and no agent registration.
  3. Impersonation of other grants — FactCheckHub (5 November 2026) rated FALSE a viral WhatsApp claim that a private foundation was paying ₦50,000 youth grants via an external short link; the foundation publicly disowned it.
  4. Provider impersonation — messages that look like OPay/Moniepoint but ask you to “reply PIN” or install an unknown APK.

Payment companies in the NERSI story have also told customers they do not decide who is eligible and will not ask for PINs or OTPs to “release” relief money.

Do this if you get a message

  • Stop — do not click first.
  • Match the sender to a provider you already use; open the official app yourself instead of a link in chat.
  • Never send BVN, NIN slip photos, or bank PIN to WhatsApp “officers.”
  • If money is demanded up front, it is not NERSI.
  • When in doubt: 0700-022-2222 (official NERSI helpline published with the launch statement).

Bottom line

NERSI is a real federal relief stream backed by ministerial statements and multi-outlet reporting. The fraud risk is equally real. Treat any “pay to be selected” pitch as hostile, keep identity secrets offline from strangers, and use only the consent path described in official SMS — or the helpline when the message feels wrong.

9jaBeacon Security / Naija Desk — based on the 30 October 2026 FMHAPR/NERSI statement as carried by Tribune, Guardian, Nairametrics and BBC Pidgin; eligibility language reported by Punch; scam pattern reference via FactCheckHub (5 November 2026).

item.title: Tenerife Striker Jesús de Miguel Dies at 30 After On-Pitch Collision in Spain
item.dc:creator: 9jaBeacon Sports Desk
item.description: CD Tenerife striker Jesús de Miguel Alameda, 30, died on 3 November 2026 after cardiac arrest following a collision with FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono. Explainer: what doctors mean by commotio cordis; tributes from RFEF, clubs and fans; investigation and family context.
item.content:encoded:
Spanish football is in mourning. CD Tenerife striker Jesús de Miguel Alameda died on the morning of Tuesday, 3 November 2026, a day after collapsing during a Segunda División home match against FC Andorra. He was 30.

The club confirmed the news in a statement issued at 08:00 local time, saying it was “heartbroken, with a lump in our throats and unable to believe that this is true.” The death has triggered tributes across Spain and beyond, a police investigation under standard procedure for non-natural deaths, and renewed debate about pitchside emergency care.

What happened on the pitch

The incident occurred in stoppage time at Estadio Heliodoro Rodríguez López in Santa Cruz de Tenerife, with the score level at 2–2. De Miguel was competing for a long ball near midfield when Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono — an Equatorial Guinea international — sprinted far from his area to clear.

In the challenge, Owono’s knee struck De Miguel in the chest. The striker collapsed. Players from both sides immediately signalled for medical help. Owono was shown a straight red card. After treatment on the field lasting several minutes, De Miguel was taken by ambulance to the intensive care unit at Nuestra Señora de la Candelaria University Hospital. The match was abandoned.

Club medical updates indicated that cardiac arrest occurred, that a pulse was restored en route to hospital, and that his condition later “worsened neurologically” before he died the following morning.

Club statement and family

CD Tenerife’s official message stressed that no words could ease the pain for his family, close friends and the club’s supporters. Reporting across Spanish and international outlets noted that De Miguel is survived by his wife and one-year-old daughter, who were at the match, and that his parents travelled to Tenerife after the incident. Funeral arrangements were discussed for the mainland, with Toledo cited in some coverage.

What is commotio cordis?

After the incident, cardiologists speaking to specialist media discussed whether a rare mechanism called commotio cordis could explain sudden cardiac arrest after a chest impact.

In plain terms: it is not a “broken heart” from emotion. It is a disruption of the heart’s electrical rhythm caused by a non-penetrating blow to the chest that lands in a very narrow window of the cardiac cycle — sometimes described as about 20 milliseconds during ventricular repolarisation. The blow may come from a ball, a knee, an elbow or another hard contact. Survival depends heavily on immediate recognition and rapid defibrillation and CPR.

Experts cited the parallel with high-profile contact-sport cases where a chest impact was followed by arrhythmia. In De Miguel’s case, reports said the impact came from the goalkeeper’s right knee. Commotio cordis remains a medical hypothesis in public commentary until forensic and clinical authorities issue final findings. It is not the same as diagnosing a long-standing structural heart disease; those possibilities are also for investigators and pathologists to address.

Investigation and emergency care questions

Spain’s National Police opened an inquiry that can include possible involuntary manslaughter — described by officials as standard when a death follows a non-natural event. Prosecutors have also been involved. Local reporting quoted the Santa Cruz de Tenerife chief prosecutor suggesting criminal proceedings were unlikely if the collision was within the normal course of play; investigators will still examine the challenge and the emergency response.

Separate questions have been raised in Spain about how quickly CPR began and whether a defibrillator was used on the pitch. Nursing and emergency-care representatives have asked for clarity against international emergency standards. Those points are under public discussion; they are not settled findings.

Who Jesús de Miguel was

De Miguel was a Spanish forward who joined Tenerife from Castellón in 2025. His path included youth football with Leganés in the Madrid area and spells with clubs such as Unionistas de Salamanca before Castellón. On the island he was a recognised first-team presence in the second tier — the kind of professional whose weekly work rarely makes global headlines until tragedy forces the world to look.

Tributes across football

The response was immediate and wide:

  • CD Tenerife published the formal death notice and asked for privacy and solidarity with the family.
  • The Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) postponed related cup fixtures scheduled for the day after his death as a mark of respect and solidarity.
  • Other Spanish clubs and stadiums observed tributes; large screens at major matches, including Champions League venues in Spain, displayed De Miguel’s image with a black ribbon.
  • Players and staff from both Tenerife and Andorra were visibly distressed on the night; the abandoned 2–2 scoreline became secondary to the medical emergency.
  • International wires and African football platforms carried the story; Nigerian outlets linked the grief to a longer list of players who died during or after matches, including the memory of Samuel Okwaraji (1989) — a comparison about the game’s shared vulnerability, not identical medical facts.

Messages of condolence from clubs, fans and federations continued through 3–4 November 2026 as funeral plans took shape on the mainland.

What remains open

  • Full medical and forensic conclusions, when released by competent authorities
  • Any formal findings on the challenge and emergency protocols
  • How Spanish football may adjust pitchside medical rules after review

Until then, the verified core is simple and heavy: a 30-year-old professional collapsed after a late collision in a competitive match, was rushed to hospital, and died the next morning. His club, his family and a wide football public are grieving.

9jaBeacon Sports Desk — synthesised from multi-outlet reporting including CD Tenerife statements as carried by AFP, AP, Punch and national Spanish coverage (3–4 November 2026). Cross-check primary club and federation updates for any later official findings.

item.title: INEC Upholds 66 of 130 Petitions on State Election Candidate Lists
item.dc:creator: 9jaBeacon National News Desk
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission said 66 of 130 petitions against its final governorship and state assembly candidate lists succeeded, while 64 failed. The commission also faces renewed pressure over irregularities in the preliminary voters register.
item.content:encoded:
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has published the outcome of its review of complaints about state-election candidate lists ahead of the 2027 polls.

According to the commission’s statement dated 29 October 2026, 66 of 130 petitions concerning the final lists of governorship and state assembly candidates were upheld. The remaining 64 petitions were rejected.

Reporting across national outlets on 30–31 October noted that the review covered petitions from multiple parties across dozens of states. High-profile outcomes included decisions affecting candidates such as former Communications Minister Isa Pantami in Gombe (appeal upheld, subject to pending court processes) and Ogun PDP aspirant Ladi Adebutu (petition not sustained).

Separately, INEC’s ICT directorate has acknowledged that some registration officers introduced irregular records—including suspected AI-generated images—into the preliminary voters register. Opposition figures including Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso and Atiku Abubakar have called for transparent audits and identification of officers involved.

9jaBeacon note: Candidate eligibility can still shift through court orders. Voters should rely on INEC’s official lists and court judgments, not social media claims.

Sources: INEC statements as reported by Channels Television, Okay News, New Telegraph and NaijaNews (31 Oct 2026).

item.title: Tinubu Nominates Six NMDPRA Executive Directors for Senate Confirmation
item.dc:creator: 9jaBeacon Business & Markets Desk
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has sent six names to the Senate for executive director roles at the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority, including three new nominees and three proposed reappointments for five-year terms.
item.content:encoded:
President Bola Tinubu has nominated six executive directors for the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA) and requested Senate confirmation.

A State House announcement dated 30 October 2026 said the six officials would serve five-year terms if approved. The package includes three new executive directors and three reappointments.

The new nominees named in national coverage are Mobolaji Tajudeen Musa (hydrocarbon processing and transportation infrastructure), Ogechukwu Modie (economic regulation and strategic planning), and Said Abutalib (corporate services and administration).

NMDPRA regulates Nigeria’s midstream and downstream petroleum markets, including infrastructure, pricing frameworks and industry compliance. Senate screening will determine whether the nominees take office.

9jaBeacon note: Nominations are not appointments until the Senate confirms them. Official confirmation notices will appear through the National Assembly and State House channels.

Sources: State House announcement as reported by Okay News and NaijaNews (30–31 Oct 2026).

item.title: Youth Forum Hails Court Decision Favoring Okorocha, Urges INEC to Recognise Him
item.dc:creator: 9jaBeacon National News Desk
item.description: The South‑East Youths Stakeholders Forum applauded Federal High Court lawyer Justice Obiora Egwuatu’s judgment declaring former governor and senatorial aspirant Rochas Okorocha the APC winner in Imo West. The forum called on INEC to register Okorocha and urged Governor Hope Uzodimma to honour the ruling ahead of the 2027 elections
item.content:encoded:
South‑East Youths Praise Okorocha After Court Ruling

According to Vanguard Nigeria, the South‑East Youths Stakeholders Forum cheered former Imo State Governor, Senator Rochas Okorocha, after a Federal High Court judgment recognised him as the All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate for the Imo West senatorial seat ahead of the 2027 general elections. The court’s decision, delivered on Thursday by Justice Obiora Egwuatu in Abuja, validated that Okorocha secured the majority of votes in the APC primary held on 18 May 2026 and called for the party to submit his name to the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC). The forum celebrated the ruling as a triumph for the rule of law and a step toward political stability in the state.

Judicial Order Demands Uzodimma Withdraw from APC Race

The judgment explicitly ordered Governor Hope Uzodimma of Imo State to cease presenting himself as the APC candidate for the Imo West senatorial election scheduled for 16 January 2027. The court found that evidence presented proved Okorocha’s majority vote, contrasting with INEC’s earlier official results that mistakenly listed Uzodimma as the primary winner—a decision that Okorocha successfully challenged in court. By directing the APC to recognise Okorocha and instructing Uzodimma to step aside, the ruling aimed to clear any confusion before the next national elections.

Youth Forum Demands INEC Compliance and Party Unity

Comrade Ifeanyi Nwosu, chairman of the forum’s Imo State chapter, issued a statement urging INEC to act upon the court’s directives and register Okorocha accordingly. He also called on Uzodimma and his supporters to respect the ruling and engage in reconciliation, stressing that unity and mutual understanding are vital for the APC’s success in the coming elections. The forum reiterated its commitment to mobilise young voters throughout the South‑East region behind President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and APC candidates, advocating collective strength over intra‑party conflict.

Implications for 2027 Election and APC Solidarity

With the court’s decree in place, the APC in Imo West must expedite the bureaucratic process of filing Okorocha’s name with INEC, aligning the party’s official stance with the judiciary. The move underscores the importance of legal resolution in pre‑electoral disputes and serves as a warning to political actors that court orders carry binding force. The youth forum’s active stance signals a burgeoning influence of young stakeholders in Nigerian politics, potentially reshaping how parties manage internal disagreements before elections. Looking ahead, the APC’s handling of this situation will influence voter confidence and could set a precedent for dispute resolution in future primaries.

Quick answers grounded in this report

1 Who was declared the APC winner in the Imo West senatorial primary?

Federal High Court Judge Justice Obiora Egwuatu declared former governor and senatorial aspirant Rochas Okorocha the winner of the APC primary for Imo West.

2 What did the court order Governor Hope Uzodimma to do?

The court ordered Governor Hope Uzodimma to stop presenting himself as the APC candidate for the Imo West senatorial election scheduled for 16 January 2027.

3 What is the role of the South‑East Youths Stakeholders Forum in this matter?

The forum congratulated Okorocha, urged INEC to recognise his candidacy, and called for Uzodimma and his supporters to respect the ruling.

Reporting based on public reporting from Vanguard Nigeria. Original source.

item.title: Federal Court Names Rochas Okorocha APC Candidate for Imo West Senatorial Seat
item.dc:creator: 9jaBeacon National News Desk
item.description: A Federal High Court in Abuja has validated former Imo Governor Rochas Okorocha as the All Progressives Congress candidate, overturning the earlier recognition of incumbent governor Hope Uzodimma. The ruling demands the party list Okorocha and bars Uzodimma from canvassing as the nominee for the 2027 senatorial election
item.content:encoded:
Judicial Verdict Sentences Okorocha to the Nomination Slot

According to Punch Newspapers, a Federal High Court in Abuja on Thursday ordered the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to publish Rochas Okorocha’s name as the All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate for the Imo West Senatorial District in the 2027 general elections. The court’s decision, issued by Justice Obiora Egwuatu, also instructs the incumbent governor, Hope Uzodimma, to cease presenting himself as the party’s nominee for the January 16, 2027 senatorial contest.

Court’s Mandate Mandates APC Action and Binding Party Listing

Justice Egwuatu directed the APC to submit Okorocha’s name to INEC as its official candidate, effectively nullifying the party’s earlier declaration of Uzodimma as the winner. The judge’s judgment was based on evidence that proved Okorocha had won the May 18, 2026 APC primary, which had been overseen by INEC. By issuing these orders, the court compellingly stalled any further campaign activities by Uzodimma and ensured that INEC’s electoral roll reflects the lawful nominee.

Primary Controversy Pits 230,000 Against 1,000 Votes

The dispute stemmed from the APC’s internal primary, where INEC’s published tally credited Uzodimma with 230,464 votes, while Okorocha was reported to have received merely 1,098. The latter result prompted Okorocha to file suit No. FHC/ABJ/CS/1854/2026, challenging the validity of the party’s recognition and questioning the incumbent governor’s eligibility to contest a senatorial election while still holding office. The court found that the primary’s outcome was indeed a misrepresentation and that the vote count should favor Okorocha against the official figures.

Implications for the 2027 Election Chronology

The ruling reshapes the political landscape for Imo West as the 2027 senatorial race approaches. With INEC now mandated to list Okorocha, the APC must adjust its campaign machinery, campaign finance, and voter outreach plans accordingly. The court’s directive also serves as a legal precedent for any future intra‑party disputes, reinforcing the principle that internal primary results must withstand judicial scrutiny before the party’s candidates can advance to the election plate. The upcoming January 16, 2027 electoral day will therefore feature a different candidate profile on the ballot than was initially established by the APC in its preliminary announcements.

Reader FAQ

Quick answers grounded in this report

1 What was the vote count difference between Okorocha and Uzodimma in the APC primary?

The APC primary results recorded 230,464 votes for Uzodimma against 1,098 votes for Okorocha.

2 What can Hope Uzodimma do after the court orders him to stop parading himself as the APC candidate?

The court ordered him to stop portraying himself as the APC candidate for the January 16, 2027 senatorial election.

3 What lawsuit led to the court’s decision?

Okorocha filed suit No. FHC/ABJ/CS/1854/2026 challenging the APC’s recognition of Uzodimma and questioning Uzodimma’s eligibility to contest while in office.

Reporting based on public reporting from Punch Newspapers. Original source.

item.title: Abia Governor Alex Otti Grants Full Scholarship to 15-Year-Old Debate Champion Esther Christian
item.dc:creator: 9jaBeacon Sports Desk
item.description: Governor Alex Otti of Abia State has awarded a full scholarship up to university level to 15-year-old Esther Christian, who led her school debate team to victory in Doha, Qatar. The gesture comes alongside monetary awards for several students and a pledge to continue investing in the state’s education sector
item.content:encoded:
Otti Grants Full Scholarship to Young Debate Champion

According to Vanguard Nigeria, Abia State Governor Alex Otti announced that 15-year-old Esther Christian has been granted a full scholarship through the Alex Otti Foundation covering all university-level studies. Christian, who lost her father at the age of four, was the captain of the Abia debate team that clinched the 2026 International Schools Debate Championship in Doha, Qatar. The governor presented the offer in front of the victorious team at the Michael Okpara Auditorium in Umuahia, signalling state support for exceptional young talent.

Generous Monetary Awards for Success Stories

During the ceremony, Otti awarded N1 million to each of the five students from Abia who represented the state and Nigeria at the international competition. He also handed N1 million to Onyinyechi Okonkwo of Ovom Girls Secondary School, winner of a recent national essay competition. Officials who accompanied the debate team received N750,000 each, while Abia Model Basic Junior Secondary School, the birthplace of the champions, received a further N1.75 million to enhance its facilities. The distribution of trophies, medals and certificates highlighted the governor’s commitment to rewarding academic excellence.

Dominant Performance in Doha’s International Schools Debate

Abia’s debate team emerged triumphant among more than 84 schools from six countries. According to Mrs Lydia Ezinne Onuoha, Chairperson of the Abia State Universal Basic Education Board, the team secured four trophies and 12 medals, including Best International School Debate Team, Overall Best Team in the Junior Category, Best Debater and Best Leadership awards. Participants faced impromptu topics and were allotted only 15 minutes to prepare and present, yet the Abian delegation topped the tournament’s speaker rankings. The victory, celebrated by the governor and other dignitaries, has opened opportunities for Nigeria to compete again in the next edition held in Singapore.

Political Endorsement and Future Commitments

Otti reaffirmed the administration’s pledge to transform Abia’s education sector through sustained investment, improved infrastructure and broader access to quality learning. He also approved the debate team’s request to participate in the 2027 edition of the competition, emphasizing that while progress has been made, continued effort is required. Other officials, including the Commissioner for Basic and Secondary Education Elder Goodluck Ubochi and the Universal Basic Education Commission Coordinator Mrs Unyime Umoette, echoed the governor’s confidence that further public office support will yield superior results for Abia’s schools.

Quick answers grounded in this report

1 How much scholarship money has Esther Christian been awarded?

Governor Alex Otti has offered a full scholarship through the Alex Otti Foundation covering all university-level studies.

2 Which other students and officials received financial awards?

Five students each received N1 million, Onyinyechi Okonkwo received N1 million, officials received N750,000 each, and Abia Model Basic Junior Secondary School received N1.75 million.

3 What achievements did the debate team earn in Doha?

They secured four trophies and 12 medals, including Best International School Debate Team, Overall Best Team in the Junior Category, Best Debater and Best Leadership awards among 84 competing schools.

Reporting based on public reporting from Vanguard Nigeria. Original source.

item.title: Federal 90‑Day Relief Plan Sparks NLC Accusation of ‘Confession, Not Cure’
item.dc:creator: 9jaBeacon Business & Markets Desk
item.description: The federal government unveiled a 90‑day relief plan to ease Nigeria’s rising cost of living, but the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) denounced it as a piecemeal confession that fails to address core economic problems. The NLC demands full transparency and concrete actions on wages, fuel prices and the national minimum wage
item.content:encoded:
Federal Government Targets 90‑Day Relief Amid Rising Cost of Living

According to Vanguard Nigeria, the Federal Government announced a 90‑day relief plan designed to provide succour to workers and the wider population in the wake of public outcry over soaring living costs. The initiative was presented as an immediate response to growing economic hardship, with the aim of easing the burden on Nigerian workers and the masses at large.

Labour Congress Brands Plan a Confession, Not Solution

NLC Assistant General Secretary Chris Onyeka slammed the plan, calling it “a confession, not a solution”. He said, “Our response to the federal government’s so‑called 90‑day plan to ease the cost of living is unambiguous. This plan is not a remedy; it is a confession.” Onyeka added that the plan “is perceptibly playing politics with the genuine cries of Nigerian workers and masses” and that the government’s past policies have afflicted Nigerians rather than improved their lives.

NLC Demands Transparency and Concrete Measures

The labour centre highlighted a lack of detail, insisting that the NLC has not seen the plan’s content. “The truth is that we have not seen the 90‑day plan or any citizen knows what it contains,” Onyeka noted. He urged the government to disclose the plan’s specifics and to take immediate action on wage awards, petroleum prices, tax relief and a review of the national minimum wage to provide tangible relief to Nigerians.

Moving Forward: Calls for Practical Action Over Empty Promises

Challenging the government’s intent, Onyeka warned that a “plan cobbled together in panic is not a plan for the people.” He called for a shift from declarative measures to sustainable solutions, stressing that the NLC’s role is to demand transparency and enforce that the public’s welfare is placed at the forefront of any policy aimed at reducing suffering and restoring purchasing power.

1 What is the 90‑Day Relief Plan announced by the Federal Government?

It is a 90‑day relief plan announced by the Federal Government aimed at providing succour to workers and the wider population in response to rising cost of living.

2 Why does the NLC criticize the plan as a confession?

The NLC claims the plan is a confession that the government’s past policies have afflicted Nigerians rather than improved their lives, and that it is not a cure for the economic hardships.

3 What demands has the NLC made regarding the relief plan?

The NLC demands full transparency about the plan’s contents, disclosure of details, and concrete actions on wage awards, petroleum prices, tax relief and a review of the national minimum wage.

item.title: TUC Rejects Federal Workers’ Proposed N70,000 Transport Allowance, Calls for Wage Justice
item.dc:creator: 9jaBeacon Business & Markets Desk
item.description: The Trade Union Congress of Nigeria (TUC) has formally rejected the federal government’s proposal to grant a N70,000 monthly transport allowance to federal workers. The union demands a rise in the minimum wage to N300,000 and equality for pensioners who were excluded from the relief
item.content:encoded:
TUC Declares No to Proposed N70,000 Transport Allowance

According to Vanguard Nigeria, the Trade Union Congress of Nigeria (TUC) rejected the government’s bid to provide federal workers with a N70,000 monthly transport allowance. The proposal had been agreed upon after a meeting between the federal government and leadership of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) on Tuesday. TUC stated that the allowance was inadequate and would not address the broader economic hardship faced by workers across the country.

Pensioners Slam Exclusion, TUC Demands Salary Rise

Meanwhile, the Nigeria Union of Pensioners (NUP) condemned the exclusion of pensioners from the transport relief, calling it “unjust” and a reminder of the cost‑of‑living crisis that retired workers also face. In its statement, TUC argued that the government has the capacity to increase the minimum wage to N300,000—four times the current rate—without waiting for a formal wage review. The union cited evidence that such a hike would substantially improve living standards for the lowest‑paid federal employees.

TUC’s Unwavering Call for Social and Economic Justice

TUC officials, including President‑General Festus Osifo and Secretary Nuhu Toro, said the union’s stance was not about “favour” but about safeguarding dignity and livelihoods. They highlighted that previous wage awards, agreed on 2 October 2023, were never fully implemented and that many workers remain unpaid for months. The union urged the government to honour its commitments, enforce the Joint Health Sector Union (JOHESU) agreement, and implement comprehensive social protection measures. “Workers’ welfare is not a privilege,” the statement read, and warned that the TUC would continue defending workers’ rights through “every legitimate avenue.”

Historical Context: Unfulfilled Wage Commitments and Ongoing Tensions

The proposed N70,000 allowance recalls the 2023 wage agreement between the federal government and organized labour, which was to be in place until a new minimum wage was set in 2024. However, the agreement was never implemented holistically, leaving some workers with unpaid dues and others without any relief. The TUC’s current rejection underscores its frustration with repeat promises that fail to materialise and its insistence that any new relief must fully meet all workers, including neglected pensioners, before it is rolled out.

Reader FAQ

Quick answers grounded in this report

1 Why did the government propose a N70,000 monthly transport allowance for federal workers?

The allowance was agreed upon after a meeting between the federal government and Nigeria Labour Congress leadership on Tuesday, as reported by Vanguard Nigeria.

2 What reason did TUC give for rejecting the transport relief proposal?

TUC said the allowance was inadequate and would not address the broader economic hardship faced by workers.

3 How did pensioners respond to the exclusion from the transport relief?

The Nigeria Union of Pensioners condemned the exclusion, calling it "unjust" and a painful reminder of the cost‑of‑living crisis for retired workers.

4 What wage increase did TUC propose instead?

TUC argued that the government has the capacity to raise the minimum wage to N300,000—the current minimum wage is N70,000.

item.title: Nigeria Boosts Transmission to 19,000MW with New East & West Super Grids
item.dc:creator: 9jaBeacon Business & Markets Desk
item.description: The federal government has commenced procurement of the East and West super grids, aiming to lift Nigeria’s transmission capacity from 5,000MW to 19,000MW in two years. This move follows the payment of N1.23 trillion of the power‑sector debt and a set of immediate upgrades to key corridors in Abuja and Lagos
item.content:encoded:
Federal Endorsement of Mega‑Grid Procurement

According to Vanguard Nigeria, the Federal Government announced yesterday the approval of procurement for the proposed East and West super grids, part of an effort to strengthen the national electricity network. The announcement was made during the end‑of‑day briefing of the Federal Executive Council (FEC) by Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, in a session presided over by President Bola Tinubu at the Presidential Villa in Abuja. Tegbe explained that the projects would improve grid resilience and enable the country to evacuate more electricity to consumers, noting that “the East and West Super Grids are not projects for one part of the country. They cut across the north and south of Nigeria, strengthening the backbone that must carry power from where it is generated to where it is needed.”

Expanding Capacity from 5,000 to 19,000MW

The initiative is designed to address one of the sector’s central contradictions: Nigeria has more than 13,000MW of available generation capacity, but its transmission network can reliably wheel only about 5,000MW. Tegbe said the super grids would improve resilience, reduce grid instability and allow more electricity to reach homes, businesses and industries. He added, “The target is simple. We want a grid that can evacuate the power we already have, not one that leaves generation stranded while consumers remain in darkness.” New corridors will strengthen transmission links from Sokoto through Abuja and other locations into parts of southern Nigeria, thereby widening the spectrum of reachable substations.

Immediate Interventions for Abuja and Lagos Corridors

Alongside the super grids, the council approved three urgent projects to support Abuja and the Lagos axis. First, a 33kV double‑circuit underground and overhead line will connect to the Katampe Transmission Substation, a major hub serving the North‑Central region. Second, it will design, manufacture and supply three 300MVA, 330/132/33kV transformers for the Ikeja West Transmission Substation, a critical node supplying Lagos. Third, it will reconstruct and upgrade the 35.6‑kilometre Itumola–Mapasin–Shagamu 132kV single‑circuit line into a double‑circuit line to serve rising demand along the Lagos–Shagamu corridor. Tegbe described them as “not glamorous projects, but they are the projects that determine whether power actually gets to the consumer.”

Debt Repayment and Future Liquidity Plans

On sector liquidity, the minister disclosed that the federal government had paid N1.23 trillion of the N3.3 trillion owed to gas suppliers and other power‑sector stakeholders. “We have paid N1.23 trillion, and we intend to finish the job. But we must also stop new debts from accumulating,” Tegbe warned. The use of the debt payment underscores the urgency for a robust transmission system that can unlock the existing power potential and prevent further financial strain on the sector.

Reader FAQ

Quick answers grounded in this report

1 What is the target capacity after the new super grids are operational?

The government aims to raise Nigeria’s transmission capacity to 19,000MW from the current approximately 5,000MW.

2 How much of the power‑sector debt has the federal government already paid?

The federal government has paid N1.23 trillion of the N3.3 trillion owed to gas suppliers and other power‑sector stakeholders.

3 Which major Nigerian cities are directly affected by the immediate interventions?

The interventions cover Abuja and the Lagos axis, including upgrades to Katampe, Ikeja West, and the Itumola–Mapasin–Shagamu corridor.

item.title: N1.35 Trillion Energy Bill Leaves 18,935 Manufacturing Jobs at Risk, CANMPEF Demands Action
item.dc:creator: 9jaBeacon Business & Markets Desk
item.description: The Chemical and Non-Metallic Products Employers Federation (CANMPEF) warned that Nigerian manufacturers spent an estimated N1.35 trillion on alternative power in 2025 and lost 18,935 jobs in the first half of the year. The federation calls on the Federal Government to cut energy, financing costs and harmonise taxes to safeguard industrial output
item.content:encoded:
Manufacturers Alarm Over N1.35 Trillion Alternative Power Bill

According to Vanguard Nigeria, delegates at the 46th Annual General Meeting of the Chemical and Non-Metallic Products Employers Federation (CANMPEF) in Lagos voiced alarm over the staggering amount that local manufacturers spent on alternative power sources in 2025, estimated at N1.35 trillion. The federation also highlighted a loss of 18,935 manufacturing jobs in the first half of the year, underscoring a dire trend in the sector.

Economic Indicators Show Growth But Manufacturing Lag

CANMPEF President Chief Devakumar Edwin presented a stark contrast between macro‑economic gains and the manufacturing sector’s performance. While Nigeria’s overall economy grew by 3.87 per cent in 2025, up from 3.38 per cent in 2024, manufacturing growth remained sluggish at 1.41 per cent, compared with 1.20 per cent the previous year. The sector’s share of real GDP fell from 8.24 per cent to 8.05 per cent, reflecting the disconnect between policy gains and factory floor productivity.

Electricity Shortfalls Drive Manufacturers to Expensive Backup

Edwin cited data from the Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission to illustrate the scale of the power crisis. Though the national grid’s installed capacity exceeds 13,000 megawatts, average delivered generation hovered below 5,000 MW against an estimated demand of approximately 18,345 MW. The resulting shortfall—attributed to gas‑supply constraints, transmission bottlenecks and recurring grid collapses—forced many energy‑intensive manufacturers to rely on costly alternative sources.

CANMPEF Calls on Gov’t to Tackle Energy and Financing Hurdles

In his speech, the federation’s vice‑president for the Dangote Group urged the Federal Government to urgently cut energy and financing costs, harmonise taxes and levies, and strengthen support for local production. He warned that without immediate intervention, macro‑economic stability would fail to translate into competitiveness, sustainable jobs, increased output and export growth for the industrial sector.

Reader FAQ

Quick answers grounded in this report

1 How much did manufacturers pay for alternative power in 2025?

Manufacturers spent an estimated N1.35 trillion on alternative power in 2025.

2 What was the manufacturing growth rate in 2025?

Manufacturing grew by 1.41 per cent in 2025.

3 How many jobs were lost in the sector during the first half of 2025?

The sector lost 18,935 jobs in the first half of 2025.

item.title: NSCDC Deputy Superintendent Nabbed for Firing Shots at Abuja Market
item.dc:creator: 9jaBeacon National News Desk
item.description: A Deputy Superintendent of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, Onoja Samuel, was arrested in Kubwa, Abuja, after firing shots into the air during a trader confrontation over reports of his wife’s assault. Police recovered a CZ pistol and 17 rounds of live ammunition, and the officer will face court proceedings
item.content:encoded:
Deputy Superintendent Arrested for Market Mayhem

According to Punch, the Federal Capital Territory Police Command on Wednesday arrested Onoja Samuel, a Deputy Superintendent with the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), after an incident that saw him firing shots into the air at a Kubwa market in Abuja. Reports said Samuel had gone armed amid allegations that traders had assaulted his wife, leading to a confrontation in which he discharged his pistol before police intervened.

Rapid Police Response on Oct. 25

Based on a statement by FCT Police Public Relations Officer Josephine Adeh, a distress call was received on 25 October 2026 at about 1:50 p.m., reporting an unidentified armed man firing sporadically at the market. Operatives from the Kubwa Police Division were deployed quickly, disarmed the suspect, and seized a CZ pistol along with 17 rounds of live 9 mm ammunition. The arrest followed coordinated efforts to neutralise the threat to traders and maintain market safety.

Commissioner Demands Inter‑Agency Coordination

FCT Commissioner of Police Ahmed Sanusi urged personnel of sister security agencies to exercise restraint and notify the police divisions responsible for the areas where they intend to conduct authorised operations. He warned that improper coordination could lead to avoidable clashes and underscored the importance of proper communication between agencies operating within the Federal Capital Territory.

Legal Proceedings and Next Steps

The NSCDC officer remains in police custody and will be charged in court after investigations conclude. The incident highlights the need for procedural controls when security officers operate outside their formal remit, and the potential repercussions for uncoordinated actions within Nigeria’s capital. The case will serve as a precedent for future security personnel conduct in publicly crowded spaces.

Reader FAQ

Quick answers grounded in this report

1 Why did Onoja Samuel go to the Kubwa market armed?

He was reportedly going to the market after hearing that traders had assaulted his wife, leading to a confrontation in which he fired at the market.

2 What was seized from Onoja Samuel during his arrest?

Police recovered a CZ pistol and 17 rounds of live 9mm ammunition from the officer.

3 Who is responsible for overseeing the investigation?

The investigation is overseen by the FCT Police Public Relations Officer, Josephine Adeh, with further steps to be taken by the FCT Police Commissioner, Ahmed Sanusi.

item.title: Rulli’s Heroic Saves Keep Donnarumma Unclouded as City Eye Quarter‑Finals
item.dc:creator: 9jaBeacon Sports Desk
item.description: Geronimo Rulli’s two penalty saves in Manchester City’s Carabao Cup tie with Brighton reassured fans that the club’s number one keeper, Gianluigi Donnarumma, remains untouchable. Manager Enzo Maresca has confirmed that Rulli’s role is defensive, not a threat to the starting spot, as City look toward next‑week’s Premier League deadline
item.content:encoded:
Heroic Penalties Resound Through City’s Stand‑Off

According to BBC Sport, Geronimo Rulli seized the spotlight in the Carabao Cup clash at Etihad Stadium when he denied Brighton’s Yasin Ayari and Lewis Dunk to secure a 3‑2 shoot‑out win for Manchester City after a 2‑2 tie in regular time. The Italian shoot‑out savior had already produced a fingertip stop to snuff out Georginio Rutter earlier, a moment that reinforced his reputation as a penalty‑time threat. Despite the pressure fans felt on Gianluigi Donnarumma, the session showed that Rulli has a narrow, well‑defined back‑up function that keeps the first‑choice free from doubt.

From Marseille to Mana United: Rulli’s Understudy Journey

Rulli’s summer move to City from Marseille for a modest £1.7 million gave him a fourth‑tier role beside Donnarumma, yet his history of high‑profile saves now reveres him as a hero‑maker. The 34‑year‑old had previously glowed in the 2021 Europa League final, netting a penalty for Villarreal before denying David de Gea to secure the trophy. At City, he spent the 2016‑17 season on the bench behind James Trafford before re‑joining the club after Leeds’ payment of £45m. City’s acquisition reflects a shrewd strategy to blend youth and experience behind the net, and Rulli’s recent clutch performances reaffirm that purpose.

Maresca‑says No Threat to Donnarumma, Just a Clear Duty

When asked if Rulli’s heroics had strained Donnarumma’s standing, Maresca told BBC Sport: “No absolutely not from my point of view. He is working well but Rulli knows exactly his role, there is no doubt about that.” The manager added that City would field Donnarumma plus ten extras for Saturday’s Premier League game against Brighton, underscoring faith in the Italian’s fitness and form. Maresca also highlighted that Donnarumma, who allowed Aston Villa’s penalty‑last goal, will receive three days of recovery before training, aiming for a reborn state for the club’s upcoming fixtures.

City’s Road to the Carabao Cup Quarter‑Finals and Wimbledon Challenges

With Rulli’s saves propelling City to the quarter‑finals, the club now faces the tactical decision of how to maximise squad depth ahead of a third‑week Premier League match against the same opponent. City’s momentum from their two‑legged Carabao Cup run will be tested as they try to maintain defensive solidity while giving chance to Rulli, who is teammates with the likes of Haaland, Dias, Anderson and Gvardiol. The club’s injuries and fatigue will drive domestic strategy decisions, but though Rulli’s performance hits the headlines, the narrative remains that the starting goalkeeper’s place is secure and that City’s focus remains winning in the league and the cup eye on Bologna and the next matchday.

Reader FAQ

Quick answers grounded in this report

1 Did Geronimo Rulli’s performance affect Donnarumma’s position in the squad?

Enzo Maresca said Rulli’s role is clear and does not threaten Donnarumma’s place.

2 What was the result of the Carabao Cup match between Manchester City and Brighton?

The match ended 2-2 in normal time and City won 3-2 on penalties, thanks to Rulli’s saves.

3 How did Rulli join Manchester City?

He returned in the summer from Marseille for a modest £1.7m to act as a back‑up to Donnarumma.

4 When will Donnarumma have his next training session after the Carabao?

He was given three days off to recover the energy and will return to training the week after the match.

item.title: Renewed Hope Ambassadors Pledge Massive Vote Drive for Tinubu in Akwa Ibom
item.dc:creator: 9jaBeacon Business & Markets Desk
item.description: A coalition of support groups in Akwa Ibom has committed to mobilising large numbers of voters for President Bola Tinubu and other All Progressive Congress candidates in the 2027 elections, according to a meeting in Uyo
item.content:encoded:
Renewed Hope Ambassadors Mobilise Massive Vote Bank for Tinubu

According to Punch Newspapers, the Renewed Hope Ambassadors – a coalition of state support groups – pledged to deliver massive votes for President Bola Tinubu across all polling units, wards and local government areas in Akwa Ibom State in the 2027 general elections. The group also vowed to back the re-election of Senate President Godswill Akpabio, Governor Umo Eno and other All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates, underscoring its comprehensive electoral agenda.

Strategic Uyo Conference Sets the Vote-Banking Agenda

During a strategic meeting held in Uyo, the state capital, the State Coordinator Prince Ikim addressed local government and ward coordinators, as well as other arms of the group. He highlighted the coalition’s commitment to mobilise voters across every polling unit and urged coordinated action. The conference was framed as a long overdue step to consolidate the party’s message of a “renewed hope” and an “ARISE” agenda.

Local Leaders Endorse Tinubu’s Economic Stewardship

Prince Ikim extolled President Tinubu’s economic reforms, citing the stabilization of the naira and the removal of the fuel subsidy as critical to averting a collapse of the economy. He praised the president’s “intentional leadership” and people‑oriented projects, particularly those benefiting Akwa Ibom. Former State House Speaker Aniekan Uko echoed this sentiment, noting that the Renewed Hope Ambassadors would actively galvanise votes for Tinubu, Akpabio, Eno and other APC contenders.

Broader APC Push Complements Statewide Vote Mobilisation

Senator Charles Mbong of the Eket Senatorial District called for extensive sensitisation to ensure voters obtain their Permanent Voter Cards, stressing that the success of Tinubu and allied candidates hinges on voter registration. The group’s pledge aligns with the APC’s broader strategy to secure votes across the country, positioning the party for a decisive win in the 2027 elections.

The Renewed Hope Ambassadors is a coalition of support groups in Akwa Ibom State that pledged to mobilise votes for President Tinubu and other APC candidates in the 2027 elections.

The group pledged support for Senate President Godswill Akpabio, Governor Umo Eno and other All Progressives Congress candidates.

The pledge was announced during a strategic meeting in Uyo, the capital of Akwa Ibom State.

item.title: Beyond the App: Africa’s Digital Economy Needs a Strong Underlying Infrastructure
item.dc:creator: 9jaBeacon Business & Markets Desk
item.description: A TechCabal panel at Moonshot 2026 underscored that African digital services must go beyond user‑facing apps to include reliable transport, connectivity, and shared infrastructure, with Nigeria’s uneven internet coverage highlighted as a key barrier
item.content:encoded:
Beyond the App: The Need for Infrastructure

According to TechCabal, the “Beyond the App: Building the Infrastructure Behind Africa’s Everyday Economy” panel at Moonshot 2026 argued that apps alone cannot scale Africa’s digital economy. Speakers stressed that the app is merely the front‑end, quoting Sanusi Adedamola, chief operating officer (COO), Fez Delivery, who said, “The app is just the front‑end,” while also representing Seun Alley, chief executive officer (CEO), Fez Delivery. The core idea is that infrastructure must support the services that apps promise.

Challenges Facing Mobility and Delivery Startups

The panel highlighted that companies in ride‑hailing, delivery, and electric mobility must tackle more than product launch. They need to ensure vehicles are available, services can locate customers via reliable location data, and operating economics remain viable in markets riddled with unreliable power, patchy connectivity, fragmented logistics, and disconnected cross‑border payment systems. These constraints raise costs, reduce reliability, and complicate expansion into new markets.

Nigeria’s Connectivity Gap Hinders Expansion

Nigeria serves as a key illustration of these hurdles. Uneven internet connectivity continues to affect businesses even in Lagos, the country’s leading commercial and technology hub. The disparity demonstrates that a robust market for digital services does not automatically guarantee the reliable connectivity required for businesses to serve customers and grow.

The Road Ahead: Building Shared Infrastructure

Panelists called for a comprehensive approach that includes reliable transport, accurate location services, access to financing, and shared infrastructure that businesses can build upon. Only by addressing these foundational elements can Africa’s digital economy move beyond superficial app adoption toward sustainable, scalable everyday services.

Reader FAQ

Quick answers grounded in this report

1 What does the panel mean by "the app is just the front-end"?

It means that beyond the user‑facing application, there must be reliable transport, location data, financing and shared infrastructure to support services.

2 Why does connectivity pose a problem in Lagos?

Uneven internet connectivity continues to affect businesses even in Lagos, the country’s leading commercial and technology hub.

item.title: Grey Unveils Paycheck Salary Account Ahead of Lagos Launch Amid Rapid User Growth
item.dc:creator: 9jaBeacon Business & Markets Desk
item.description: Grey, the Y Combinator-backed payments firm, introduced Paycheck, a salary management tool for U.S. dollar, Pound, and Euro earners, at its Moonshot 2026 event in Lagos, aiming to expand beyond three million users. The platform promises higher savings rates, increased limits and priority support while streamlining cross‑border earnings for professionals
item.content:encoded:
Launch at Moonshot Signals Expansion Target Beyond Three Million Users

According to TechCabal, Grey, the start‑up that has processed nearly $5 billion in payments since 2020, rolled out Paycheck – a dedicated salary account – during the Moonshot by TechCabal 2026 event in Lagos on Wednesday. The announcement comes as the company recorded a 170% year‑on‑year rise in total payment volume and set a new goal to grow its user base beyond its current three million members.

CEO Highlights the Critical Role of Salary Management

Idorenyin Obong, Grey’s co‑founder and chief executive officer, underscored the importance of salary in life planning, stating, "After a month of work, employees should have more to look forward to than the additional responsibility of sorting through transactions and keeping track of their earnings." He added that "a salary is central to how people meet their needs, plan ahead, and build financial security," and that the company’s services should mirror that significance.

Automated Transactions and Attractive Benefits Power Paycheck’s Appeal

Paycheck allows users to receive and manage salaries in U.S. dollars, British pounds and euros, automatically organising all related transactions. The product also offers higher interest rates on savings, increased transaction limits and priority customer support. Existing Grey customers who receive salaries can activate Paycheck without altering any account details, while new users can simply share their Grey account information with employers or payroll providers; activation occurs after their next qualifying payment.

From Currency Exchange to Recurring Income Service: Grey’s Future Roadmap

Founded in 2020 by Obong and Femi Aghedo, Grey evolved from a currency‑exchange platform into a comprehensive cross‑border payments provider for individuals and businesses. The Paycheck launch marks a strategic move to embed the company deeper into the financial lives of professionals by offering tools centered around recurring foreign‑currency income, positioning it for sustained growth in the Nigerian and global fintech landscape.

Reader FAQ

Quick answers grounded in this report

1 Will existing Grey users need to change their account details to activate Paycheck?

Existing customers can activate Paycheck without changing their account details.

2 Which currencies can users manage with Paycheck?

Paycheck supports salaries paid in United States dollars, British pounds, and euros.

3 What benefits does Paycheck provide?

Paycheck offers higher interest rates on savings, increased transaction limits and priority customer support.

item.title: AU Recognises Nigeria’s Counter‑Terrorism Centre as Regional Hub for West Africa and Sahel
item.dc:creator: 9jaBeacon National News Desk
item.description: The African Union has accredited Nigeria’s National Counter Terrorism Centre (NCTC) as a Regional Centre of Excellence, expanding its mandate to provide training, joint threat analysis and technical assistance to member states. The move follows a rigorous assessment and aligns with President Bola Tinubu’s vision of a regional counter‑terrorism platform
item.content:encoded:
AU Names NCTC a Regional Counter‑Terrorism Hub

According to Vanguard Nigeria, the African Union (AU) has officially accredited the National Counter Terrorism Centre (NCTC) – operating under the Office of the National Security Adviser (ONSA) – as a Regional Centre of Excellence in Counter Terrorism for West Africa and the Sahel. The decision, announced at the conclusion of the African Lessons Learned Forum in Abuja on 27 October 2026, fulfils President Bola Tinubu’s vision set out in the High‑Level African Counter‑Terrorism Meeting in April 2024 to position the NCTC as a regional hub for intelligence sharing, operational coordination and specialised training against terrorism and violent extremism.

New Mandate Expands Training and Co‑ordination Across West Africa

The accreditation grants the centre an expanded regional mandate to provide specialised training, joint threat analysis, research, technical assistance, exchanges of lessons‑learned and other counter‑terrorism support to AU member states, especially those in West Africa and the Sahel. According to the statement issued by the NCTC’s Head of Strategic Communication, Abu Michael, the designation marks a significant milestone in Nigeria’s contribution to collective African security and formally positions the NCTC to support regional partners through enhanced counter‑terrorism cooperation and institutional capacity development.

Rigorous Assessment Trail From MOA to Final Approval

The accreditation process began with the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding between the AU and the NCTC in September 2025, followed by a technical assessment mission conducted by the African Union Counter‑Terrorism Centre (AUCTC) in December 2025. The mission produced an accreditation roadmap that outlined the institutional standards required for recognition. Since then, the NCTC has strengthened governance structures, developed training curricula and operational procedures, improved analytical and coordination functions, and reinforced its commitment to human rights and the rule of law. Acting Director of the AUCTC, Dr. Idriss Mounir Lallali, praised the NCTC’s collaborative efforts with ONSA, its leadership, personnel and strategic partners, noting that the successful completion of the accreditation requirements reflected the centre’s institutional development and the rigorous assessment undertaken by the AU.

Strategic Significance for Nigeria and the Sahel

Lallali announced that the AU will formally convey the decision to the Government of the Federal Republic of Nigeria through a Note Verbale from the Department of Political Affairs, Peace and Security. The accreditation is expected to enhance Nigeria’s role as a security fulcrum in the region, enabling the NCTC to conduct joint trainings, threat‑analysis workshops and capacity‑building initiatives with neighbouring countries. The move also underscores Nigeria’s commitment to regional stability and the broader African agenda of countering terrorism through cooperation, knowledge sharing and adherence to human‑rights norms.

Reader FAQ

Quick answers grounded in this report

1 What does the accreditation mean for other West African members?

The accreditation grants the NCTC a mandate to provide specialised training, joint threat analysis, research, technical assistance and exchanges of lessons learned to AU member states, especially those in West Africa and the Sahel.

2 When was the Memorandum of Understanding signed?

The Memorandum of Understanding between the AU and the NCTC was signed in September 2025.

3 Who announced the accreditation?

The Act‑Director of the African Union Counter‑Terrorism Centre, Dr. Idriss Mounir Lallali, announced the accreditation on 27 October 2026 in Abuja.

4 Which office within Nigeria leads the NCTC?

The National Counter Terrorism Centre operates under the Office of the National Security Adviser (ONSA).

item.title: Governor Fubara Calls Rivers Monarchs to Exercise Neutrality Ahead of 2027 Elections
item.dc:creator: 9jaBeacon National News Desk
item.description: In a meeting of 126th, 127th and 128th Combined Quarterly Session of Rivers State Traditional Rulers, Governor Sir Siminalayi Fubara urged leaders to stay neutral and enforce peace as the 2027 elections approach, promising to honour their stipends and uphold constitutional oaths
item.content:encoded:
Governance Meets Tradition Amid Election Countdown

At a bustling gathering in Port Harcourt, the 126th, 127th and 128th Combined Quarterly Meeting of the Rivers State Council of Traditional Rulers unfolded beneath the watchful eyes of the state's governor. The assembly, framed by the tradition of communal justice, served as a platform for the leader to remind the monarchs of their vital role against a backdrop of rising political activity.

Prime Minister-Level Ruling on Neutrality Set Before 2027 Election

According to Punch Newspapers, Governor Sir Siminalayi Fubara declared the session open and explicitly cautioned the chairmen, elders and princes to maintain neutrality and promote fairness as the nation marched toward the 2027 general elections. He highlighted that the conduct of rulers should not spark division or crisis, stressing that their influence could either stabilize or unsettle the state’s social fabric.

Balancing Oaths, Constitution and State Stability

Fubara reiterated that the traditional rulers’ primary duties are to administer justice and uphold the constitution they swore to uphold before taking the stool. He urged them to set aside personal sentiments, placing the collective interest of Rivers State above individual agendas, and reminded them that the oath is integral to sustaining peace and progress. The governor also cited the statutory benefit of stipends paid by Local Government Councils, emphasizing that any delays stemmed from the council’s internal shortcomings rather than governmental will.

Promises to Implement Stipends and Future Policy Steps

Reaching a pledge of fidelity, the governor confirmed his readiness to fulfil promises to the royal fathers, underscoring his adherence to his word and his practical governance style. He signed off by affirming that the constitution, oath and earnest action toward the welfare of stakeholders would uphold his administration’s path toward unity and sustainable development for Rivers State, as the upcoming elections loom large.”

1 Why are traditional leaders asked to remain neutral during the elections?

Governor Fubara warned that their conduct should not lead to division or crisis, urging the rulers to promote peace and uphold fairness in the lead-up to the 2027 elections.

2 How does the governor plan to support the traditional rulers?

Fubara reaffirmed that stipends, a constitutional benefit paid by Local Government Councils, will be reinstated and that he remains committed to fulfil his promises to the royal fathers.

item.title: ALTON Calls for Elimination of Telecom Right‑of‑Way Fees, Citing Up to 60% Cost of Fiber Deployment
item.dc:creator: 9jaBeacon Business & Markets Desk
item.description: The Association of Licensed Telecommunications Operators of Nigeria (ALTON) has urged state governments to abolish right‑of‑way charges for telecom infrastructure, arguing that the fees can account for up to 60% of fiber‑optic deployment costs and hinder network expansion into underserved areas. The association proposes free access and strategic use of the Universal Service Provision Fund to facilitate broader coverage
item.content:encoded:
ALTON Demands Vanquishing of Right‑of‑Way Fees to Spur Broadband Expansion

According to Vanguard Nigeria, the Association of Licensed Telecommunications Operators of Nigeria (ALTON) has called on state governments to scrap right‑of‑way charges that hinder the rollout of fiber‑optic networks. The calls were made by ALTON Chairman Engr. Gbenga Adebayo during a plenary session at the 2026 Nigerian Economic Summit in Abuja, where the issue was highlighted as a major impediment to broadband access in rural and underserved communities.

Right‑of‑Way Charges Erode Up to 60% of Fiber Deployment Costs

ALTON pointed out that, in some states, the cost of obtaining right‑of‑way approvals can be as high as 50 to 60 per cent of the total cost of deploying a kilometre of fiber. The association warned that this fee structure disproportionately affects operators’ willingness to invest in areas where anticipated revenue fails to cover the entire infrastructure outlay, effectively stalling expansion into communities with poor or no connectivity.

Legislative Reform and Incentives: A Blueprint for Affordable Expansion

Engr. Adebayo called for legislation that would make right‑of‑way access for telecommunications infrastructure free, especially in rural communities and other areas where commercial returns are expected to be minimal. He also urged the government to introduce incentives for operators investing in high‑cost, low‑revenue zones and to employ the Universal Service Provision Fund (USPF) more strategically to support network growth in these underserved locations.

Strategic Use of USPF and Future Investment Priorities

The chairman emphasized that the existing USPF is intended for special intervention where coverage is lacking, and that deployment costs exceeding potential revenue should be met with targeted support. He argued that the issue is largely economic, not a lack of willingness to invest, and that improved policy and incentive frameworks would enable operators to extend service to communities currently missing broadband connectivity. ALTON also underscored the need for increased investment in fiber‑optic cables, telecommunications sites, and network capacity to further enhance service quality across Nigeria.

Reader FAQ

Quick answers grounded in this report

1 Why do right‑of‑way charges deter telecom operators from expanding in rural areas?

Right‑of‑way fees can represent up to 60% of the total cost of deploying fiber, making investments in low‑revenue zones economically unviable for operators.

2 What mechanisms is ALTON proposing to support network expansion?

ALTON urges free right‑of‑way access and targeted use of the Universal Service Provision Fund to subsidize high‑cost, low‑revenue deployments.

3 Which government event highlighted ALTON’s concerns?

Engr. Adebayo made the appeal during a plenary session at the 2026 Nigerian Economic Summit in Abuja.

Reporting based on public reporting from Vanguard Nigeria. Original source.

item.title: Actress Doris Ogala Remanded Over Alleged Cyberstalking of Pastor Chris Okafor
item.dc:creator: 9jaBeacon National News Desk
item.description: Federal High Court in Lagos has remanded actress Doris Ogala to Kirikiri Correctional Centre as she faces charges of cyberstalking, cyberbullying and attempted extortion against Pastor Chris Okafor. The case, stemming from alleged publication of intimate photos and false messages, is set for an accelerated bail hearing
item.content:encoded:
Judge Orders Remand Amid‑Stubborn Charges Against Actress

According to Punch Newspapers, the Federal High Court in Lagos on Wednesday remanded actress Doris Ogala to the Kirikiri Correctional Centre pending a hearing on her bail application. Justice Akintayo Aluko ordered the remand after Ogala pleaded not guilty to three counts of cyberstalking, cyberbullying and attempted extortion filed by the Office of the Attorney‑General. The court held that the defence had not supplied enough material to justify her release, thereby setting an accelerated date for the bail trial.

Allegations Focus on Publication of Intimate Images and False Messages

The prosecution, led by counsel Tolulope Mokolu, alleged that between September 2024 and March 2026 Ogala published nude and intimate photographs of Pastor Chris Okafor on her social media accounts without consent. Mokolu further claimed the actress disseminated videos, recordings, and electronic messages that she knew to be false, with intent to bully, threaten and harass the cleric. In addition, the prosecution pointed to threats that Ogala would continue to release menacing and intimate material unless Okafor provided compensation or purchased a house. These charges were said to contravene Sections 24(1)(a), 24(2)(a) and 24(2)(c) of the Cybercrimes (Prohibition, Prevention, etc.) Amendment Act, 2024.

Bail Plea Sparks Urgent Judicial Review

Following her plea, defence counsel N. C. Atulomah argued that Ogala, a governorship candidate in Abia State, would attend future hearings and urged the court to grant bail. However, Justice Aluko deemed the defence’s submission insufficient and directed an accelerated hearing of the bail application. The judge also ordered Ogala’s remand at Kirikiri while the prosecution awaited the opportunity to file a response, as the bail application was received only on the day of the proceedings.

Political Implications Heighten Public Interest in the Case

The case now sits at the intersection of criminal law and political ambition, as Ogala’s political affiliations add a layer of scrutiny. It is scheduled for an additional adjournment until October, where the court will decide on bail and set a trial date. The outcome will influence both the legal proceeds of the alleged cyber offences and the political trajectory of a candidate whose future hinges on the court’s final decision.

Reader FAQ

Quick answers grounded in this report

1 Was Doris Ogala found guilty of the alleged offences?

No, she pleaded not guilty to the three counts and is awaiting a bail hearing.

2 What law was cited in prosecuting her?

Sections 24(1)(a), 24(2)(a) and 24(2)(c) of the Cybercrimes (Prohibition, Prevention, etc.) Amendment Act, 2024.

3 When will the next court hearing be?

The case is adjourned until October for the determination of the bail application.

4 What did the defence claim about Ogala’s political status?

She was a governorship candidate in Abia State and would attend the next hearing.
