item.title: APC Pushes Back Against Claims That Ministers Pay Billions for Appointments
item.dc:creator: 9jaBeacon Business & Markets Desk
item.description: The All Progressives Congress (APC) denied allegations that ministers pay billions of naira to secure positions, insisting spokesperson Alwan Hassan’s remarks were references to past practices rather than the current administration. The party’s National Publicity Secretary, Felix Morka, further questioned how such purported payments could be recovered within Nigeria’s budgetary framework
item.content:encoded:
APC Denies Ongoing Corruption Claims

According to Vanguard Nigeria, the All Progressives Congress (APC) denounced assertions that ministers are paying billions of naira to obtain appointments. Party officials emphasised that the remarks attributed to APC’s Presidential Campaign Council spokesperson, Alwan Hassan, were not indicative of contemporary practices. Instead, they described historical tendencies that predate the party’s current alliance.

Alwan Hassan’s Arise TV Remarks Contextualised

In an interview with Arise TV, Hassan said, “A lot of ministers pay billions and billions, and, you know, to get themselves appointed. The first thing they think of is how to recoup that money.” He further noted, “What he was referring to was not really about this administration, but he was speaking in historical context.” These statements were presented to illustrate past behaviours rather than ongoing issues within the current APC-led administration, according to the source.

Felix Morka Calls for Clarity and Defends Current Administration

National Publicity Secretary Felix Morka, speaking on Primetime, questioned how ministers could recover alleged sums within Nigeria’s budgetary framework. He said, “If ministers are paying billions to get appointed, how exactly, within what we know to be Nigeria’s budgetary frame, do you recoup the billions you paid to get appointed?” Morka stressed that Hassan’s comments were historical and not a critique of the present government, adding that they “did not necessarily mean that the current administration is corrupt.” He highlighted that in other democracies, lobbying is commonplace, but monetised lobbying is “not unusual.”

The Path Forward: Historical Reform and Transparency

The party’s position moves toward reaffirming accountability and transparency while distinguishing past improprieties from current operations. By insisting that ministers’ alleged financial dealings “predate APC,” APC seeks to distance itself from the allegations and emphasize its commitment to reform. The incident prompts a broader discussion about the need for clearer legislation on appointment processes and the role of lobbying in Nigerian politics. As the nation waits for the next electoral cycle, the APC’s clarifications may shape public expectations for ethical governance moving forward.

Reader FAQ

Quick answers grounded in this report

1 Did the APC confirm that current ministers do not pay for appointments?

The party said the comments made by Alwan Hassan referred to historical practices, not the present administration.

2 What did Felix Morka say about the financial feasibility of alleged payments?

Morka questioned how ministers who allegedly paid billions could recoup those sums within Nigeria’s budgetary framework.

3 Did the APC compare Nigerian practices to other democracies?

Morka noted that lobbying for appointments is common in other democracies, implying that such activities are not unique to Nigeria.

Reporting based on public reporting from Vanguard Nigeria. Original source.

item.title: Kwankwaso Alerts INEC on Suspected AI‑Generated Voter Images, Urges Transparent Audit
item.dc:creator: 9jaBeacon National News Desk
item.description: Former Kano governor Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso has warned the Independent National Electoral Commission about possible AI‑generated photographs in the 2027 voter register, demanding a public, independent review. He insists that the 2027 elections’ legitimacy hinges on a trustworthy register
item.content:encoded:
Veteran Politician Raises Red Flag Over Voter Register Integrity

According to Vanguard Nigeria, former Kano State Governor and senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso posted a statement on his personal Facebook page warning the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) about alleged irregularities in the preliminary voter register that could jeopardise the credibility of the 2027 general elections. He cited reports of suspicious photographs that may have been generated using artificial intelligence, noting that any failure to investigate could erode public confidence in Nigeria’s electoral system ahead of the election cycle.

Allegations of AI‑Generated Photographs and Questionable Entries

Kwankwaso highlighted that the health of the 2027 electoral process depends on “a credible voter register” and that the discovery of potential AI‑fabricated images raises serious questions about the integrity of the registration process and the safeguards INEC has implemented to prevent manipulation. He asked how such photographs could have entered the register, whether those listed are genuine voters, and whether their identities were properly verified. Kwankwaso urged the Commission to conduct a thorough, transparent, and independent investigation, insisting that findings be made public and that those found culpable be held accountable under law.

Demand for an Independent Audit and Protection of Voting Rights

Beyond the immediate investigation, the former governor called for a comprehensive independent audit of the preliminary voter register to spot questionable entries, duplicate registrations and possible artificial identities. He stressed that this audit must take place without denying any eligible Nigerian the constitutional right to vote. “Our democracy cannot afford any compromise in the integrity of the voter register. Every eligible Nigerian must have the right to vote, and every vote must count,” he added. His remarks aim to safeguard the electoral outcome by ensuring each vote’s legitimacy.

Implications for the 2027 Election and Future Safeguards

Kwankwaso warned that the credibility of the 2027 general elections largely depends on the accuracy of the voter list and cautioned against the use of emerging technologies, especially artificial intelligence, to undermine the electoral process. He said, “Nobody should be allowed to exploit technology, including artificial intelligence, to undermine our electoral system.” The former governor’s call for decisive action signals a push for stronger vigilance and more robust verification protocols as INEC prepares for nationwide voting.

Reader FAQ

Quick answers grounded in this report

1 What prompted Kwankwaso to address the alleged AI-generated images in the voter register?

The former governor raised his concerns following reports of suspected artificial intelligence-generated photographs and other questionable records in the register, as stated in his Facebook post.

2 What does Kwankwaso want INEC to do regarding the voter register?

He urges INEC to conduct a thorough, transparent, and independent investigation, release findings publicly, hold those responsible accountable, and carry out a comprehensive audit that does not deny eligible Nigerians their voting rights.

3 Why does Kwankwaso emphasize the role of technology in this issue?

He warned against the use of emerging technologies, particularly artificial intelligence, to manipulate the electoral process and stressed that such exploitation should not undermine Nigeria’s electoral system.

Reporting based on public reporting from Vanguard Nigeria. Original source.

item.title: Government Approves N45.08bn Biosecurity Upgrade for Nigeria’s Five Major Airports
item.dc:creator: 9jaBeacon Business & Markets Desk
item.description: The Federal Government has earmarked N45.08bn for a 20‑year public‑private partnership to install a national biosecurity and response system across Abuja, Lagos, Kano, Port Harcourt, and Enugu airports. The move comes amid heightened concern over cross‑border infectious diseases and the need to protect both public health and economic stability
item.content:encoded:
State House Confirms Record‑Breaking Biosecurity Budget

According to Punch Newspapers, the Federal Government on Wednesday approved a N45.08bn investment in a national biosecurity and response system that will be implemented across five international airports. The decision was announced by Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. (Prof.?) Ali Pate, during a briefing with State House correspondents following a Federal Executive Council session chaired by President Bola Tinubu. The budget allocation aims to strengthen Nigeria’s capacity to detect and contain infectious diseases at its borders.

A 20‑Year PPP Framework Anchors the Initiative

The budget will be channelled through a 20‑year public‑private partnership arrangement with the Biohealth Consortium, a consortium of partners experienced in health technology solutions. The consortium will be responsible for the design, procurement, installation, and maintenance of the biosecurity infrastructure at the selected airports. The partnership model, according to Pate, shortens the time required for deployment while ensuring sustainability and expertise across the lifespan of the project.

Targets Five Major Gates Amid Rising Health Vigilance

Under the approved plan, the Kofo Akuku system will cover the Murtala Muhammed International Airport, Lagos; Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja; Mallam Aminu Kano International Airport, Kano; Port Harcourt International Airport; and the Akanu Ibiam International Airport, Enugu. The project followed two years of preparation and was justified against the backdrop of over 18 million passengers passing through Nigerian airports annually. Pate highlighted that strengthening biosecurity at points of entry is vital not only for public health but also for economic security, noting that disease outbreaks can severely disrupt economic activity.

Implications for Traveler Flow and Economic Stability

As part of the broader health security agenda, the government also defended its policy of compensating quarantined individuals with N100,000 per week to ensure compliance with isolation directives amid a recent Ebola case. The new biosecurity system is expected to provide technology‑driven, early warning, detection, and response mechanisms that will reassure travelers and airlines, thereby preserving the flow of international passengers and safeguarding Nigeria’s economic interests, especially given the high volume of passenger traffic across the five airports.

Reader FAQ

Quick answers grounded in this report

1 Which airports will receive the new biosecurity system?

The Murtala Muhammed Airport in Lagos, Nnamdi Azikiwe Airport in Abuja, Mallam Aminu Kano Airport in Kano, Port Harcourt International Airport, and Akanu Ibiam Airport in Enugu.

2 How long will the public‑private partnership last?

The partnership will span 20 years under the Biohealth Consortium.

3 What is the total cost of the project?

The federal government approved a sum of N45.08bn for the program.

4 Why has the government paid N100,000 per week for quarantined persons?

It is to secure compliance with isolation directives amid a recent Ebola case.

item.title: Flutterwave Bags Microfinance Licence to Take Control of Payments Stack
item.dc:creator: 9jaBeacon Business & Markets Desk
item.description: Flutterwave secured a national microfinance banking licence after buying open‑banking startup Mono, expanding beyond payment processing to store deposits, lend and offer banking services. CEO Olugbenga Agboola said the move gives the firm deeper control over its infrastructure and new loan‑origination possibilities
item.content:encoded:
TechCabal Reports Flutterwave’s Bank Licence Milestone

According to TechCabal, in April Flutterwave, the pan‑African fintech unicorn, secured a national micro‑finance banking licence by acquiring open‑banking startup Mono. The licence allows the company to hold deposits, provide credit and run other banking services, moving it into a new category of regulated financial institutions on the continent.

Acquisition of Mono Paves the Way for Micro‑Finance Operations

With the Mono deal, Flutterwave now controls a critical part of its payments infrastructure. The company has processed more than $40 billion in lifetime payments and serves over 2 million businesses. By owning its own banking licence, it can manage the payment stack end‑to‑end and avoid dependence on third‑party banks that might fail or deviate from its standards.

Peers Follow: Paystack and Moniepoint Enter Regulated Banking

Flutterwave is not alone. In January, Paystack acquired Ladder Microfinance Bank, and Moniepoint secured a micro‑finance banking licence in 2025. These moves mark a growing trend of Nigerian fintechs turning from mere payment processors into regulated banks, seeking to deepen service offerings and capture larger shares of the financial ecosystem.

CEO Stresses Control and Depth Over Payment Convenience

Olugbenga “GB” Agboola, co‑founder and CEO of Flutterwave, explained at the Moonshot conference in Lagos that the licence was chosen to “control more of the infrastructure behind its payments business.” He noted, “What we’ve seen is you cannot provide a great payment experience if you don’t control the entire stack, or at least a big piece of the stack.” The move also opens a path into lending, where transactional data from its payment platform could give the company a competitive edge in assessing credit risk and offering working capital to merchants.

Reader FAQ

Quick answers grounded in this report

1 How many businesses use Flutterwave’s payment platform?

More than 2 million businesses use the platform

2 Why did Flutterwave acquire Mono?

To control more of the infrastructure behind its payments business and avoid dependence on third‑party banks

3 What new services can Flutterwave offer after the licence?

It can now hold deposits, provide credit and offer other banking services

item.title: Atiku Demands Daily Proof of President Tinubu’s Umrah under Scrutiny Over France Link
item.dc:creator: 9jaBeacon Business & Markets Desk
item.description: Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has publicly challenged President Bola Tinubu to show daily evidence of his presence in Makkah for Umrah, alleging the trip could mask a flight to France. The dispute centers on questions about a reported $20 billion loan involving a French business partner and the president’s health
item.content:encoded:
Atiku’s Public Challenge Unfolds

According to Vanguard Nigeria, former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has issued a public challenge to President Bola Tinubu, demanding daily proof of the president’s presence in Makkah during an alleged Umrah pilgrimage. Atiku alleges that the trip could be a smokescreen for an unpublicised visit to France, prompting him to call on the presidency to release verifiable, date‑stamped photographs and videos of Tinubu performing the rites in front of the Kaaba.

Financial Ties Raise Red Flags

Atiku highlighted a reportedly $20 billion loan request that the president is pursuing with a French business partner. He stressed that the high value of the loan, coupled with the secrecy surrounding the itinerary, warrants full disclosure. The former vice president said Nigerians deserve to know whether the trip is linked to the president’s health or to secure critical funding for the loan, urging the Presidency to publish a transparent account of the trip’s activities and funding sources.

Calls for Transparency and Accountability

Beyond photographic evidence, Atiku urged the presidency to provide a comprehensive, day‑by‑day itinerary of the president’s movements while in the Holy Land, including any stop in France. He warned that invoking Almighty Allah in political discourse without sincerity could erode public trust, emphasizing that a spiritual mission on behalf of the nation must be conducted with accountability. The former vice‑president added that both he and other Nigerians would join Tinubu in prayers if the trip proves genuine, but cautioned against using religion as a cover for political or financial maneuvers.

Awaiting Official Response

No official statement from the presidency has yet been released in response to Atiku’s challenge. The controversy has reignited discussions about transparency in state affairs, especially when state actors are involved in substantial foreign financial dealings. Observers note that the situation may affect public perception of executive integrity and could influence forthcoming assessments of the president’s appropriateness to lead the country. Any forthcoming clarification will be closely watched by the Nigerian public and international partners alike.

Reader FAQ

Quick answers grounded in this report

1 Has President Tinubu confirmed his presence in Makkah during the alleged Umrah?

No official confirmation has been released at the time of the report, and the presidency has not responded to Atiku’s request.

2 What is the exact amount of the reported loan?

The reported loan amount is $20 billion, as cited by Atiku in his challenge.

3 What reasons does Atiku give for suspecting a trip to France?

Atiku says intelligence suggests a brief appearance in Makkah followed by a subsequent trip to France.

item.title: TCN Arrests Over 30 Suspected Vandals in Kano‑Kaduna Corridor, As Community and Police Join Forces
item.dc:creator: 9jaBeacon Sports Desk
item.description: According to Punch, the Transmission Company of Nigeria (TCN) secured more than 30 arrests for vandalism along the Kumbotso‑Zaria line, spotlighting the rising threat of encroachment on transmission towers. The operation, carried out in partnership with residents, traditional authorities and security agencies, aims to protect the infrastructure that supplies power over 200‑300 kilometres
item.content:encoded:
TCN Seizes Over 30 Vandals Along Kano‑Kaduna Corridor

According to Punch, the Transmission Company of Nigeria (TCN) arrested more than 30 suspected vandals who had targeted electricity infrastructure along the Kumbotso–Zaria transmission line corridor. The arrests were announced by the company’s Kano Regional General Manager, M.K. Bello, during a sensitisation campaign held in the Paki community, Ikara Local Government Area of Kaduna State, on Wednesday, 28 October 2026. The operation reflects growing concerns over the integrity and safety of the 200‑to‑300‑kilometre‑long high‑voltage lines that keep the region powered.

Community Campaign Sheds Light on Rising Encroachment

During the campaign, Mr. Bello warned residents about the dangers posed by excavation, construction activities and the digging of pits in close proximity to transmission towers. He noted that improper excavation can weaken these structures and potentially lead to tower collapse. The event, attended by district head Ja’afaru Paki and other traditional leaders, generated a call for community vigilance and reports of suspected vandalism to authorities.

Legal Action Trend: Ten Towers Vandalised in 2026

M.K. Bello revealed that ten transmission towers had been vandalised in the past four to five months of 2026. He added that the company has five active cases pending in court over these incidents. According to Bello, damage to even a single tower can disrupt power supply and require expensive replacement, underscoring the importance of swift legal action and preventive measures.

Cooperation with Traditional Rulers and Police Fuels Success

Bello credited the arrests to collaborative efforts between TCN, residents, traditional rulers, the district head, the police and other security agencies. He expressed gratitude for the community’s support, noting that their cooperation was instrumental in protecting the transmission infrastructure. As part of the initiative, TCN urged residents to avoid activities that could endanger towers and to report any suspicious activity to the appropriate authorities.

TCN arrested more than 30 suspected vandals along the Kumbotso‑Zaria transmission line corridor.

2 What legal action has TCN taken against the vandalism cases?

TCN has five cases pending in court over the vandalism incidents.

3 Who supported TCN in the arrest operation?

Traditional rulers, the district head, the police and other security agencies supported TCN.

item.title: SDP Counters INEC Postponement Fears, Deems 2027 Elections Secure
item.dc:creator: 9jaBeacon National News Desk
item.description: The Social Democratic Party’s national leadership dismissed rumours that INEC might delay the 2027 general elections, citing no credible evidence to support such fears. SDP Publicity Secretary Araba Rufus Aiyenigba emphasised readiness of the commission and refuted security and health concerns that could impact the polls
item.content:encoded:
SDP Refutes Postponement Rumours Amid INEC Allegations

According to Vanguard, the national leadership of the Social Democratic Party (SDP) stated there is no reason to fear that the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) will postpone the 2027 general elections. Speaking to the outlet on Wednesday, SDP National Publicity Secretary Araba Rufus Aiyenigba said, “For the SDP, there is no justifiable reason to entertain fears that the Commission could be tempted to postpone the scheduled 2027 general elections.” The party contested claims that INEC was planning to shift the January 16 vote date.

Health Concerns Dismissed by NCDC as Ebola Weaponization Claims Fall Flat

The SDP added that the public‑health scare linked to alleged Ebola reports has been dismissed by the Nigerian Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC). The party also rejected claims that Ebola was being weaponised, noting that health authorities strongly refuted such allegations. Aiyenigba’s remarks imply that the health narrative poses no credible threat to the electoral timetable.

Security Gridlock and Electoral Act Inaction Re‑addressed by INEC Online Measures

Security crises, often cited as a basis for election postponement, “are yet to be in a dimension of grave concerns,” the party said. It also addressed worries about the Electoral Act 2026, particularly the delay in displaying the voters’ register, by pointing to INEC’s response: the commission has uploaded the preliminary voters’ register online on its portal. This move, SDP officials argue, alleviates doubts regarding election readiness.

SDP Stays Vigilant, Pledges Support for Fair 2027 Democracy

While maintaining vigilance, the SDP remains optimistic that nothing will impede the 2027 general elections. Aiyenigba pledged that the party would keep its “eyes on the ball,” underlining its commitment to ensuring the polls are held, seen as fair, and credibly conducted, in line with the nation’s best interests.

Reader FAQ

Quick answers grounded in this report

1 Why does the SDP believe INEC will not postpone the elections?

The SDP National Publicity Secretary stated there is no justifiable reason to entertain fears that the Commission could be tempted to postpone the scheduled 2027 general elections.

2 What does the SDP say about the Ebola allegations?

The SDP reiterated that the Nigerian Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) dismissed the public‑health scare and that claims of Ebola being weaponised were strongly rejected by health authorities.

INEC responded by uploading the preliminary voters’ register online on its portal, countering worries about delays in displaying the register.

item.title: FG Approves Super-Grid Projects to Boost Nigeria's Power Trans‑mission to 19,000MW in Two Years
item.dc:creator: 9jaBeacon Sports Desk
item.description: The Federal Government plans to launch procurement of the East and West Super Grids, aiming to lift national transmission capacity from 5,000MW to 19,000MW. Three immediate interventions for Abuja and Lagos will also accelerate power flow to critical demand hubs
item.content:encoded:
Federal Government greenlights super‑grid procurement

According to Vanguard Nigeria, the Federal Government on Wednesday approved the commencement of procurement for the proposed East and West Super Grids, part of a drive to strengthen the national electricity network. The initiative is designed to increase transmission capacity from roughly 5,000 megawatts to 19,000MW within two years. The approval came after a briefing of State House correspondents at the conclusion of the Federal Executive Council (FEC) meeting presided over by President Bola Tinubu at the Presidential Villa in Abuja.

Minister Joseph Tegbe outlines transformative grid plan

Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, explained that the super‑grids will cut across northern and southern Nigeria, building a resilient backbone that transports power from generation hubs to consumers. He highlighted that Nigeria’s 13,000MW of available generation is bottlenecked by a transmission network that only reliably wheels about 5,000MW. “We want a grid that can evacuate the power we already have, not one that leaves generation stranded while consumers remain in darkness,” Tegbe said. The corridors would also tie Sokoto to Abuja and further south, addressing grid instability and enabling more electricity to reach households, businesses and industries.

Immediate upgrades for Abuja–Lagos axis spotlighted

Alongside the super‑grid plans, the council approved three targeted interventions for the Abuja–Lagos electricity corridor, sectors with the highest demand. First, a 33kV double‑circuit underground and overhead line will link the Katampe Transmission Substation, a key hub for the North‑Central region. Second, the procurement of three 300MVA, 330/132/33kV transformers for the Ikeja West Transmission Substation will bolster Lagos supply. Third, the 35.6‑kilometre Itumola–Mapasin–Shagamu 132kV single‑circuit line will be upgraded to a double‑circuit line to meet rising demand along the Lagos–Shagamu corridor. Tegbe noted the importance of these projects, stating they directly determine whether power reaches consumers.

Challenges and next steps: manufacturing, audit, timeline

Minister Tegbe admitted that Nigeria still lacks domestic capacity to manufacture the large, high‑capacity transformers required for the West‑Mexico West‑Congo Super Grids, stating these units must be assembled abroad. Although some companies have begun local assembly, specialised manufacturing takes three to six months, with global demand rising thanks to artificial intelligence and data centres. The ministry has also launched a nationwide technical audit of electricity infrastructure to inform future procurement and upgrade decisions. The procurement process will be public, ensuring transparency as the government pursues its goal of a more reliable and high‑capacity power grid.

Reader FAQ

Quick answers grounded in this report

1 What is the timeline for the transmission capacity upgrade?

The government aims to increase capacity from about 5,000MW to 19,000MW within two years.

2 Which areas will the super‑grids connect?

The super‑grids will cut across northern and southern Nigeria, also linking Sokoto to Abuja and further south.

3 Where will the transformers for Lagos be produced?

They must be manufactured abroad because Nigeria does not yet have the domestic capacity for that specification.

4 How will the immediate Abuja–Lagos upgrades improve power supply?

They include a 33kV double‑circuit line to Katampe, three large transformers for Ikeja West, and a double‑circuit upgrade of the 35.6‑km Itumola–Mapasin–Shagamu line.

item.title: Mutfwang Launches Tinubu Door‑to‑Door Brigade in Plateau Ahead of 2027 Election
item.dc:creator: 9jaBeacon Sports Desk
item.description: Plateau Governor Caleb Mutfwang has inaugurated the state's 2027 support group for President Bola Tinubu, unveiling 25 campaign vehicles and signalling strong state‑level backing. The launch also highlighted federal infrastructure projects and set the stage for a major rally in Zaria on November 14
item.content:encoded:
Launch of PBAT Plateaus Chapter Reveals 25 New Campaign Vehicles

According to Punch, Wednesday’s inauguration of the Plateau State Chapter of the PBAT Door‑to‑Door Movement marked the formal start of grassroots support for President Bola Tinubu’s 2027 re‑election bid. Held at the Langfield Event Centre in Little Rayfield, Jos, the ceremony featured the unveiling of 25 campaign vehicles donated by the movement’s Grand Patron, Chief Government Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo, to boost mobilisation across the state.

Governor Names Meeting with Tinubu as Catalyst for Support

Speaking at the event, Governor Caleb Mutfwang revealed that his decision to back Tinubu stemmed from a personal meeting with the president shortly after the 2023 general elections. "I made up my mind that this was the President to work with even when I was not in the same party with him. I saw a man who is committed to making Nigeria better," he said, underscoring his confidence that federal‑state collaboration would address security and economic challenges.

Federal Front‑End Interventions Highlighted in Road‑Infrastructure Push

Mutfwang cited ongoing federal work on the dualisation of the Mararaban Jam’a‑Mangu‑Pankshin‑Langtang‑Shendam corridor, a project aimed at clearing stalled road development for decades. A technical team from the Federal Ministry of Works is already carrying out preliminary studies in the state, and the governor expressed optimism that project details would be finalised before year end, promising improved connectivity and economic activity for local communities.

November Rally Targeted at Mobilising 50 Volunteers per Camp

As part of the campaign build‑up, Mutfwang announced that Plateau State will host President Tinubu for a major rally at Zaria Road Stadium on November 14, 2026. He urged movement members to recruit at least 50 participants each to attend the rally, signalling an aggressive grassroots push designed to cement Tinubu’s 2027 ticket.

The dualisation of the Mararaban Jam'a‑Mangu‑Pankshin‑Langtang‑Shendam corridor, with a technical team already conducting preliminary work.

He is slated to return next week after completing the sacred rites, having also commissioned new Nigerian Air Force equipment beforehand
item.content:encoded:
Tinubu’s Journey to Makkah Begins

According to Vanguard Nigeria, President Bola Tinubu will depart Abuja on Thursday for Makkah, Saudi Arabia, to perform Umrah, an Islamic pilgrimage that includes a series of prayers and religious rites. The move comes amid a period of national reflection, with the president intending to spend the week in prayer for Nigeria’s future.

Spiritual Intentions Highlight Peace Amidst National Goals

The president’s Special Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, stated that Tinubu’s visit will provide a chance for spiritual reflection and prayers for Nigeria’s peace, unity, stability and continued progress. While in Makkah, the leader is expected to seek Allah’s guidance and blessings for the nation and its people, a gesture that underscores his commitment to secular legislative outcomes and inclusive governance.

Domestic Preparations Ahead of the Pilgrimage

Before departing, Tinubu is set to commission equipment acquired by the Nigerian Air Force at the Presidential Wing of the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport. This commission reflects ongoing military procurement and modernization efforts and is a ceremonial act reinforcing the president’s role in supporting national security initiatives.

Timeline and Expected Homecoming

President Tinubu is slated to return to Nigeria next week after completing the spiritual exercise. The statement detailing the itinerary was dated October 28, 2026, indicating a ten‑day trip that bridges his domestic duties with religious observance.

President Tinubu is expected to return to Nigeria next week after completing the spiritual exercise.

item.title: Rivers State Court Seeks Judge’s View on APC’s Eligibility to Contend in 2027 Governorship Election
item.dc:creator: 9jaBeacon National News Desk
item.description: A Federal High Court petition, lodged by the Peoples Redemption Party, argues that the APC should be barred from fielding a candidate in Rivers State’s February 2027 governorship poll. The suit hinges on alleged non‑compliance with Section 77 of the Electoral Act and a recent Supreme Court ruling that might invalidate APC’s primaries
item.content:encoded:
Petition Files a Legal Challenge to APC’s Nomination

According to Vanguard Nigeria, the Federal High Court in Port Harcourt has received a petition (FHC/PH/CS/193/2026) asking the court to declare that the All Progressives Congress (APC) is ineligible to field a candidate for the 2027 Rivers State governorship election. The suit, brought by the Peoples Redemption Party (PRP) and its gubernatorial aspirant, Hon. Kieghe Nature Dumale, also requests that the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) remove the APC and its candidate from the list of parties approved to contest on 6 February 2027.

Supreme Court Judgment Sparks Alleged Breach of Electoral Law

In an 18‑paragraph affidavit, Dumale asserted that on 24 September, the Supreme Court delivered a judgment (Appeal No. SC/CV/495/2026) concerning INEC and the Zenith Labour Party. The ruling addressed the constitutionality of Sections 77(5)‑(7) of the Electoral Act, 2026, and reaffirmed INEC’s authority to enforce compliance and sanction parties that fail to meet those provisions. Dumale claims that the APC did not satisfy the requirements laid out in Section 77(5)‑(7) for its gubernatorial primaries, thereby violating the law and undermining the court‑mandated compliance process.

INEC’s Published Candidate List Raises Legal Questions

After the Supreme Court decision, INEC Chairman Prof. Joash Amupitan announced that the Commission would review the ruling. However, the court was told that INEC did not evaluate the APC’s records before publishing a final list of parties and candidates. A press release issued on 13 October stated that, pursuant to Section 287(1) of the 1999 Constitution, and following the Supreme Court’s decision, INEC had excluded parties that did not meet Section 77(5)‑(7) when finalising the candidates for the governorship poll. The court lists Exhibit ‘A’ as the published list and Exhibit ‘D’ as the APC’s Register of Members for Ward 3(B), Obio/Akpor, submitted on 20 April 2026.

Implications for APC and the Upcoming Election

Should the court rule in favour of the petition, the APC would be formally prohibited from presenting a candidate in the 2027 Rivers State governorship election, effectively removing the party from the ballot paper. This decision would follow a controversial series of primary elections that the APC scheduled to start on 15 May, after sending its Register of Members to INEC on 20 April. The ruling could also prompt a re‑evaluation of candidate lists for the February 6 election, potentially altering the political landscape in the state and setting a precedent for enforcing compliance with Electoral Act provisions across Nigeria.

Reader FAQ

Quick answers grounded in this report

1 Why has the APC been challenged to be disqualified from the 2027 election?

The petition alleges that the APC failed to comply with Sections 77(5)‑(7) of the Electoral Act, 2026, and that the Supreme Court’s recent judgment confirms the validity of such compliance requirements.

2 What role did INEC play in the controversy?

INEC published a final list of candidates following the Supreme Court's ruling, excluding parties that did not meet Section 77(5)‑(7) compliance, a move that the court questioned for lacking prior review of the APC’s records.

3 What will happen if the court sides with the petition?

The APC would be officially barred from fielding a candidate in the 2027 Rivers State governorship election, and its name would be removed from INEC’s list of eligible parties.

item.title: Chief of Miden Systems Honoured as He Warns of Deepfake Threats Ahead of 2027 Elections
item.dc:creator: 9jaBeacon Business & Markets Desk
item.description: The Federal Government awarded Dr Brendan Innocent Usoro, executive chairman of Miden Systems, for corporate governance while he cautioned against AI‑generated misinformation that could undermine Nigeria’s 2027 elections. His speech at the NPC summit highlighted how deepfakes can erode public trust and urged tighter cooperation between tech firms and regulators
item.content:encoded:
Awarded for Integrity Amid Rising Misinformation

According to Vanguard Nigeria, the Federal Government presented Dr Brendan Innocent Usoro with an award for business integrity during the Nigerian Press Council (NPC) National Summit on Curbing Fake News and Misinformation. The ceremony, held in Abuja on Tuesday, was organised by the Federal Ministry of Information and National Orientation and brought together media practitioners, government officials, corporate executives and security agencies to discuss ways of combating misinformation and promoting responsible journalism.

Usoro Voices Alarm Over AI‑Generated Deepfakes

Speaking at the event, Usoro warned that the growing use of artificial intelligence to generate fake audio recordings, manipulate videos and circulate fabricated reports had made it increasingly difficult for the public to distinguish facts from falsehoods. He stated, "People use false information to de‑market their political opponents, competitors’ products and services, as well as create tension in the polity," adding that deepfakes and coordinated disinformation campaigns could manipulate voters, erode public trust and undermine democratic institutions ahead of the 2027 elections.

Miden Systems’ Own Battle with False Claims

Usoro disclosed that Miden Systems had suffered damaging effects from false information following a financial dispute with a commercial bank. He highlighted the company’s evolution from safety and equipment maintenance services in 1997 to a diversified entity involved in marine services, logistics, offshore and onshore facility upgrades and management, and noted its major oil and gas contracts with organisations such as Renaissance Africa Energy Company.

Call to Action: Verification and Cooperation

To tackle misinformation, Usoro urged Nigerians to verify information before sharing it and recommended independent fact‑checking platforms, including Dubawa. He called for improved training for journalists and fact‑checkers, wider access to AI‑assisted verification tools, and stronger collaboration between technology companies and regulatory agencies such as the National Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA) and the Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC). He cautioned that efforts to curb misinformation must not compromise press freedom, freedom of expression or legitimate criticism.

He was honoured at the Nigerian Press Council National Summit on Curbing Fake News and Misinformation, held in Abuja on Tuesday.

He cited fake audio recordings, manipulated videos and fabricated reports that make it difficult for the public to distinguish facts from falsehoods.

He mentioned Dubawa as an independent fact‑checking platform.

He urged collaboration with the National Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA) and the Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC).

item.title: Dickson Demands INEC Probe into Alleged AI‑Generated Voter Entries
item.dc:creator: 9jaBeacon National News Desk
item.description: Senator Seriake Dickson has called on the Independent National Electoral Commission to investigate potential AI‑generated photographs and fictitious names in the 103‑million voter register ahead of the 2027 general elections. He warns that a flawed database could erode public trust and Nigeria’s international standing
item.content:encoded:
Dickson Demands INEC Probe into Possible AI‑Generated Voter Entries

According to Vanguard Nigeria, National Leader of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Senator Seriake Dickson, has urged the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to urgently investigate claims that artificial intelligence may have generated photographs and problematic entries in its preliminary voter register. Dickson described the allegations as a serious matter requiring prompt attention, warning that failure to validate the data could undermine confidence in Nigeria’s 2027 general elections.

NDC Leadership Meets Dickson Amid Calls for Transparency

During a meeting in his Abuja residence on Wednesday, Dickson welcomed the National Coordinator of the Dickson Movement for Democracy, Comrade Ogbidi Emmanuel, and other members of the group. They formally presented the organisation to him, and he was decorated as its Grand Patron. The session included a call for INEC to not merely issue statements but to actively safeguard the integrity of the voter register.

Authenticity Questions Cast Doubt on 103‑Million Register

The NDC leader stressed that Nigerians deserve assurance that the roughly 103 million registrations announced by the commission represent genuine, verifiable enrollments of eligible citizens. He warned that the database might include fictitious identities, photographs of deceased persons, or images of individuals who are not eligible voters, which could damage both INEC’s credibility and Nigeria’s international reputation.

INEC Must Deliver Clear Fix, Citizens Encouraged to Verify Registrations

Dickson called on INEC to provide a clear explanation and establish the facts surrounding the allegations, taking all necessary measures to clean up the register. He urged Nigerians to use the statutory display of the voter register at designated locations to scrutinise entries and report any suspicious or inaccurate information, giving the commission time before the elections to address the concerns.

The article states that INEC may have issued a response but must go beyond statements and address the concerns.

Approximately 103 million registered voters have been announced by the commission.

item.title: Kano Police Foil Kidnapping Plot, Arrest Two Suspects

item.description: When village head Mallam Idris received a threatening call, the Kano State Police Command acted swiftly to arrest two 20‑year‑old suspects who had plotted to kidnap him. The arrests were confirmed by the command’s spokesperson, and police urged the public to report suspicious activity
item.content:encoded:
Threatening Call to Village Head Sparks Inquiry

According to Punch Newspapers, the village head of Bangare Village, Mallam Idris, reported a threatening phone call on 26 October 2026 at about 01:30 hrs to the Gezawa Divisional Police Headquarters. The call, received on 24 October at approximately 21:33 hrs, came from an unknown number and warned of a planned kidnapping. The report prompted an immediate response from operatives attached to Gezawa Division, marking the start of a security operation that would later lead to arrests.

Rapid Arrests of Two 20‑Year‑Old Suspects

The Kano State Police Command confirmed that two suspects, Aliyu Naziru Garba, 20, and Bashir Alhasan, 20, were detained for criminal conspiracy and criminal intimidation. CSP Abdullahi Haruna, the command’s Public Relations Officer, stated that sustained follow‑up coupled with intelligence‑led operations resulted in the arrests. Both suspects confessed to the alleged plot, and the investigation is ongoing, with an expectation that they will be charged to court once formal proceedings commence.

Police Commendation and Zero‑Tolerance Stance

Police Commissioner Ibrahim Adamu Bakori praised the Gezawa Division officers for their “swift and professional response.” He reiterated the command’s zero‑tolerance policy for all forms of criminality and highlighted the importance of community cooperation in maintaining security. The commission’s statement underscored a collective commitment to thwart future threats against local leaders.

Public Vigilance Urged Amid Ongoing Investigation

The Kano police call on residents to remain security consciousness and to report suspicious persons or movements. Communications can be made through the command’s emergency lines: 08032419754, 08123821575, or 09029292926. The ongoing investigation will culminate in court proceedings where the suspects will face charges linked to the kidnapping threat.

item.description: Police in Kano state halted an alleged kidnapping scheme targeting the village head of Bangare, arresting two 20‑year‑old men who confessed to the plot. The operation, praised by state officials, underscores the command’s commitment to curb local violence
item.content:encoded:
Kidnap Threat Sparks Rapid Police Response

The Kano State Police Command arrested two 20‑year‑old men on Friday night after the village head of Bangare, Mallam Idris, reported receiving a death threat. The suspects, Aliyu Naziru Garba and Bashir Alhasan, were accused of plotting to abduct Mallam Idris in Gezawa Local Government Area. The organisation of the alleged abduction had drawn a swift police reaction as the threat escalated concern over the safety of local traditional leaders.

Gezawa Division Launches Overnight Raid

According to Vanguard Nigeria, Mallam Idris telephoned the Gezawa Divisional Police Headquarters at about 1:30 a.m. on October 26. He said an unidentified caller had threatened to kidnap him two days earlier. Promptly, police operatives attached to the division launched an operation that culminated in the arrest of Garba and Alhasan early in the morning. The suspects later confessed to the crime, according to Police Public Relations Officer CSP Abdullahi Haruna Kiyawa.

Command Praises Officers, Highlights Ongoing Investigation

Commissioner of Police in Kano State, Ibrahim Adamu Bakori, commended the officers for their swift action and professional handling of the case. He reiterated the command’s commitment to tackling criminal activities across the state. Kiyawa reported that investigations remain ongoing and the suspects will be charged in court once the inquiry concludes. The police also urged residents to remain alert and report any suspicious persons or movements to their nearest station.

Community Remains on Guard, Authorities Promise Follow‑Up

The arrest has reinforced local security protocols, with authorities stressing the importance of vigilance among community members. Residents are reminded to report any threats or unusual behaviour, as the Kano Police Command stands ready to intervene. While the suspects are yet to face court, the swift move is seen as a deterrent against future attempts to target traditional leaders in the region.

item.title: Moonshot Lagos: Gates Foundation Urges Nigeria to Build AI around Real‑World Impact
item.dc:creator: 9jaBeacon Business & Markets Desk
item.description: During a Moonshot event in Lagos, Gates Foundation’s Director for Nigeria, Uche Amaonwu, warned that Nigeria’s AI progress should be measured by improved lives rather than product counts. He urged the nation to build reliable foundations and practical applications in key sectors to unlock significant economic value
item.content:encoded:
Moonshot Debate: AI Measured by Human Impact

According to TechCabal, Uche Amaonwu, Director of the Gates Foundation Nigeria Country Office, spoke at the Moonshot forum in Lagos on Wednesday, insisting that "Nigeria’s artificial intelligence (AI) ambitions should be judged by the lives the technology improves." He criticised the prevailing metric of simply counting AI products, calling it a distraction from the real test of “whether people are going to be able to use these AI solutions and tools, whether there is an institution that can sustain those tools over time, and whether we actually see better outcomes from the use of those tools.”

From Healthcare to Agriculture: Nigeria’s AI Roadmap

During the same session Amaonwu highlighted four priority sectors – healthcare, education, agriculture and public services – as the next phase for AI deployment in Nigeria. He cited a McKinsey & Company study estimating that generative AI could generate between $61 billion and $103 billion of economic value across African markets. The Gates Foundation’s 2026 Goalkeepers report echoed this, arguing that AI could become a great equalizer by expanding access to knowledge and services, provided deliberate interventions are made to avoid widening existing inequalities.

Solid Foundations Required for AI Adoption

Emphasising infrastructure, Amaonwu drew a parallel to Nigeria’s fintech growth, stating that it thrived thanks to robust payments infrastructure, clear regulation, appropriate policy and institutions ready to adopt technology. "AI is going to need similar foundations for us to be able to replicate what happened with fintech," he said, adding that reliable connectivity, trusted data, and interoperable systems were critical. Without these, he warned, each innovator would face the same basic challenges, stalling nationwide adoption.

AI as Equalizer or Divider? 2026 Goalkeepers Insight

Amaonwu further warned that many advanced AI models are built outside Africa and trained on data that may not capture local languages or experiences, limiting their usefulness. He urged Nigeria to cultivate AI models that reflect its own realities while leveraging Gates Foundation support to promote equitable use of AI. The overarching message: with the right foundations and purposeful focus, AI could transform Nigeria’s public services and drive inclusive growth, but failures in implementation could worsen disparities.

Reader FAQ

Quick answers grounded in this report

1 What sectors did Amaonwu say Nigeria should focus on for AI deployment?

Healthcare, education, agriculture and public services.

2 What economic value could generative AI unlock in Africa, according to the source?

Between $61 billion and $103 billion.

3 What infrastructure does Amaonwu compare to fintech for AI success?

Reliable connectivity, trusted data, and systems that can interoperate.

4 Why does Amaonwu caution against using global AI models?

Because they may not reflect local languages or experiences and could limit usefulness.

item.title: "Emergency on Security, Education, Power" – Obi Promises Drastic Shifts If Elected
item.dc:creator: 9jaBeacon Business & Markets Desk
item.description: NDC presidential hopeful Peter Obi vows a health‑check style takeover of security, schooling and electricity, demanding a state of emergency if he wins a 2027 presidential election. The former governor outlined concrete plans to deliver 10,000 MW of power and free, compulsory education, while chastising President Bola Tinubu’s overseas absences
item.content:encoded:
Obi Drives ‘Emergency’ Promise for Security, Education, Power

According to Vanguard Nigeria, the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, announced that he would declare a state of emergency in security, education and electricity if elected president in 2027. He made the pledge during a town hall meeting with supporters and grassroots stakeholders in Kwanga, Nasarawa State, where he outlined plans to improve security, expand access to education and boost electricity generation.

Power Goals: 10,000 MW Within Four Years

The former governor of Anambra State promised to deliver 10,000 megawatts of electricity within four years of an NDC administration, describing reliable power supply as critical to industrialisation and job creation. This figure, if achieved, would represent a significant increase over the current national supply and the NDC’s focus on infrastructure development.

Critique of Tinubu’s Overseas Absence and Call for Presence

Obi criticised the present administration, alleging that President Bola Tinubu had spent more than 260 days abroad since assuming office while Nigerians grappled with economic hardship and insecurity. He said, "Nigeria wants a leadership that will be available to all Nigerians, not a President that sits in Abuja or travels abroad while the country burns." The former governor further argued that borrowing should be directed towards productive investments rather than corruption and consumption.

Grounded Campaign and Grassroots Engagement in Nasarawa

During the meeting, Obi highlighted the NDC’s strategy of travelling across the country to engage directly with voters, rather than conducting campaigns from Abuja. The NDC vice‑presidential candidate, Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, described the party as belonging to all Nigerians and urged voters to participate actively in the 2027 elections. In Nasarawa, the NDC chairman, Dogo Shammah, noted the state as Obi’s political home, citing strong grassroots support shaping the party’s national strategy.

According to Vanguard Nigeria, Obi pledged to declare a state of emergency in those areas if elected president to accelerate reforms.

item.title: WHO Advises No Gathering Restrictions as Nigeria Combats Ebola Case
item.dc:creator: 9jaBeacon National News Desk
item.description: The World Health Organization has decided not to impose gathering limits after a single Ebola case in Nigeria, citing swift containment measures. With 53 contacts monitored, the country must remain disease‑free for 42 days to declare the outbreak over
item.content:encoded:
WHO Counters Rumours with No Restrictions on Public Gatherings

The World Health Organization (WHO) announced on Wednesday that it has not advised the Nigerian federal government to restrict public gatherings following the confirmed Ebola case in the country. The agency emphasised that the decision was based on technical assessment rather than political pressure, highlighting that its guidance came after evaluating the country’s response mechanisms.

Prototype Response Strategy: 42 Days of Disease‑Free Peace and 53‑Person Surveillance

According to Vanguard Nigeria, the WHO stated that Nigeria would need to remain free of additional Ebola cases for a consecutive 42‑day period before it could be declared Ebola‑free. In the interim, 53 individuals who had contact with the patient have been placed under continuous surveillance and daily follow‑up to detect any secondary transmission early.

Fast‑Track Lab Confirmation and Medical Evacuation Explained

Dr Chikwe Ihekweazu, WHO’s Executive Director of the Health Emergencies Programme, clarified on Arise TV that the patient’s medical evacuation was conducted at the request of her country of origin and reflected no deficiencies in Nigeria’s case management capacity. He praised the speed of laboratory confirmation, sequencing and overall containment, describing the nation’s response as “commendable” and “excellent.”

Key Next Steps: 21‑Day Follow‑Up and Sustained Technical Support

The senior WHO official stressed that every contact must be monitored daily, with a 21‑day follow‑up phase followed by an additional 21 days to ensure no further spread. WHO pledged to continue technical support, urging Nigerians to trust state agencies and adhere to the coordinated response plan until the 42‑day window elapses.

Reader FAQ

Quick answers grounded in this report

1 Why has WHO opted not to impose gathering restrictions in Nigeria?

WHO has not advised the Federal Government to restrict public gatherings after the single Ebola case, citing that the country’s containment measures have been effective.

2 What does the 42‑day requirement for Nigeria mean?

Nigeria must report no new Ebola cases for a continuous 42‑day period before it can be declared Ebola‑free.

3 How is the 53 contacts being monitored?

All 53 individuals who had contact with the patient are under surveillance and daily follow‑up for 21 days, then an additional 21 days to detect any transmission early.
